It also holds state:visualizer’s other pages, docs/{beans,todos,health, issue-marks,swimlane-glossary,uploads}/index.html, each headed “Generated by scripts/state-visualizer.ts”. docs/uploads/index.html is the viewer OF uploads/, not an upload, and the uploads refusal’s **/uploads/** would catch it; first match wins, so the viewer entries sit above the refusal. docs/fsh-guts/index.md is not committed: it is derived from fsh-guts/, which is kept on a branch, so it is built at publish by derive:publish and a merge cannot meet it. That is the general answer for any derived page whose input lives on a branch — see directory-conventions §”The storage clock” — and is better than a take-base pattern, which only makes the collision cheap. The archive itself (fsh-guts/**) is kept content and stays refused. viewer-namespace — take the base, regenerate . docs/cat-harness/{catalogue,folio,library,schemas,uploads,voices}/**: the pages gen-library-viz, gen-folio-viz and gen-schema-viz place through viewerPlacement, each rewritten whole from the corpus and checked by its :viz --check. As above, its uploads/ pages render uploads rather than being them. auto-docs/ under the same prefix keeps its own auto-docs entry. navbar-include — take the base, regenerate . docs/_includes/generated/**: the navbar/footer include written whole by gen-navbar-include.ts (navbar:include --check). Any new page, graph or tile rewrites it. Its authored neighbours in docs/_includes/ stay refused. viewer-nav-qa — take the base, regenerate . test/results/viewer-nav/viewer-nav.qa.json: check-viewer-nav’s mechanical layout verdict over every viewer page. Recomputed from the pages, and it carries no reviewer’s attestation. handler-index — take the base, regenerate . docs/cat-harness/published-graphs.md, the handler’s index of every published graph and declared viewer, written whole by gen-handler-index.ts (handler:index:check). Any new graph or viewer rewrites it. skos-glossary-export — take the base, regenerate . **/docs/assets/glossary/*.skos.jsonld: the published SKOS export, written whole by glossary:export (glossary-export.ts, gated by glossary:check). Every layer’s export restamps whenever any declared role, skill or term moves, so two PRs that touch unrelated skills still collide here. It is not the ledger, and that distinction is the whole safety argument. glossary-ledger.json carries forward: glossary-export.ts reads the prior ledger and preserves a concept’s earlier names as skos:hiddenLabel, so taking one side would drop a term’s history. The ledger sits one level up from generated/ and matches no glob here — verified, and pinned by a test. This is .gitattributes’s rule applied to a resolver: the test is not is it generated but does its producer carry anything forward.skos.jsonld does not match site-data’s cat-harness/docs/assets/**/*.json — .jsonld is not .json — which is why it needed its own entry rather than falling through. glossary-generated — take the base, regenerate . **/glossary/generated/**: the per-instance generated glossary JSON, same writer and same check as skos-glossary-export. The glob stops at generated/, so the sibling ledger is untouched. skill-instructions — take the base, regenerate . **/docs/reference/skill-instructions/**: skill instruction bodies, written whole by skills:docs (gen-skill-docs.ts’s OUT_DIR, gated by skills:docs:check). Never hand-edit it. Safe because emit() is compare-or-write with no merge — under --check it compares and records drift, otherwise it writes the content whole — so nothing is carried forward from the file on disk. The authored neighbour is the skill itself. skills/**/*.md is the SOURCE these pages are generated from and stays refuse; a test pins that pair, because resolving the generated copy while taking a side on the source is the mistake this entry would otherwise invite. docs-pages — take the base, regenerate . The cat-harness/docs/**.md pages gen-docs-pages.ts writes whole from the authored blocks under cat-harness/docs/source/<slug>/ (docs:pages, gated by docs:pages:check). Each one says so in its own front matter: . generated: scripts/gen-docs-pages.ts — do not hand-edit; run `bun run cat docs:pages` . Safe because nothing is carried forward. emit() is compare-or-write: the only read of a prior page is inside its --check branch, for the comparison, and every other read in the script is of an INPUT (readBlock over docs/source/, BPMN XML, manifests). Its one walk of the output directory skips files carrying the generated marker. Confirm the writer by reading the script, not by how whole-file it looks. Gated on EXACT content, which is why take-base is verifiable rather than merely convenient. The generator’s own docblock says a difference in a page is “somebody who added a node, renamed a block, ran a first sweep, or moved a sidecar, and did not regenerate”. So after take-base, docs:pages:check proves the regenerated page is right — the resolution is not trusted, it is checked. The slugs are ENUMERATED, not globbed, and that is deliberate. cat-harness/docs/*.md and guides/ mix generated pages with authored ones (architecture.md, index.md, agent-onboarding.md, …). A directory glob would take a side on authored prose — the one thing a resolver must never do. The cost is that a page added to docs/source/ is refused until its slug is declared here, which is the safe direction to be wrong in, and a test reads the pages’ own front matter from the TREE so the enumeration cannot go quietly stale. That test must read the front matter, not the file: the generated body of this skill, docs/reference/skill-instructions/merge-conflict-patterns.md, quotes the marker in the code fence above, and a detector that reads a quotation as a declaration finds its own documentation (audit-coverage). That page’s front matter names gen-skill-docs.ts, and skill-instructions is declared before docs-pages, so the first match gives it the right owner. The authored neighbour is the source, and it stays refused. cat-harness/docs/source/process-publication-workflow/every-workflow-in-the-repo.md is the hand-written INPUT for docs/process/publication-workflow.md. Even when both sides only added rows, a union of additions is a property of that layer and not of the path. A test pins the pair, and pins that nothing under content/ is claimed at any depth. health-report — take the base’s measurement . test/health/results/*.health-report.json. Not a derivation of the tree but a measurement of external state (publish branch, clone size, the work plan), written by bun run cat health and refreshed daily on the base by the health-check workflow, so the base’s copy is simply the newer measurement and a branch’s older one carries nothing worth keeping. check:harness-state judges its producer hash; if the merge changed the producer, bun run cat health rewrites it. qa-witnesses — take the base, regenerate . test/results/witnesses/**: witness projections (qa-witness/v1) and page verdict indexes, written by gen-docs-pages.ts from the kg-qa sidecars and the live subject. A projection, never an attestation, and the docs-site build regenerates them at publish. pot-templates — take the base, regenerate . translations/**/*.pot: gettext templates extracted from the English pages by pot-for-pages.ts (translation:pot:check), so every edit to a source page rewrites its template in every locale. The .po files beside them are authored translations and stay refused. site-data — take the base, regenerate . Generated site data indexes under docs/assets/**/*.json and docs/_data/. subgraph-index and subgraph-payload — owned tree, regenerate . **/docs/subgraph/** holds the subgraph JSON-LD indexes. **/docs/payload/sha256/** holds the content-addressed payloads (<hex> is the sha256 of its bytes, with a <hex>.json sidecar beside it). bun run cat subgraph:jsonld writes both directories whole, and it deletes every file in them that it did not write. Any skill edit rewrites an index and moves a payload. Why not take-base. When both sides change one node’s payload, git reads it as a rename/rename. The base’s hex goes to the branch’s hex on one side and to main’s hex on the other. Git leaves the old name at stage 1 only, the branch’s new name at stage 2 only, and main’s at stage 3 only. Both new stages hold git’s three-way merge of the two bodies, with conflict markers. So take-base fails in two ways: . | It reads “stage 2 only” as “the base deleted it” and git rms the branch’s new payload. That is a path the branch added, so droppedInMerge refuses it at the resolved checkpoint. | checkout --theirs writes marked bytes under a name that is the hash of other bytes. | . The owned-tree strategy (takeOwnedTree in merge-base.ts) reads the parents’ commits, never the stages. For each path: . | it takes the base’s committed blob when the base has the path; | it takes the branch’s committed blob when only the branch has it; | it removes the path only when neither parent has it, which is a deletion both sides made. | . The resolution therefore drops nothing a parent holds, and every kept payload holds the bytes its name hashes. The orphan it keeps is the writer’s to remove. The writer is named in the pattern as prunedBy: "subgraph:jsonld", a writer and not a check: regen still derives the check from the CI workflow. When regen runs that writer, the writer deletes the orphan. Both droppedInMerge checkpoints still hold, and they are why this works. The resolved checkpoint sees no drop. The staged checkpoint sees the writer’s deletion of the superseded payload, a path the branch added, and allows it because the disk no longer holds it either. That is the legitimate replacement of a content-addressed payload, which a single post-regen check would have refused. The test fixture in merge-base.test.ts covers this, and so does its refusal sibling, which shows that take-base on the same merge is refused. Adding another owned-tree pattern needs a writer that deletes what it did not write. Without one, the kept orphan survives regen, and only the writer’s :check can catch it. The test requires every owned-tree pattern to name a prunedBy script that has a :check twin. Under --no-regen (a merge train), the orphan stays in the member’s merge commit until the train’s final regen. navbar-rail-data — owned tree, regenerate . **/docs/assets/navbar/rail-*.js is the navbar’s shared rail data. Each file is named rail-<hash>.js after the content hash of the rail JSON it carries (lib/harness-rail.ts), so a changed rail is a new file and the old one is orphaned. bun run cat navbar:assets deletes every rail file no committed page names, and navbar:assets:check fails on one. Both sides of a merge add their own hash, which is why this is owned-tree and not take-base, for the same reason as subgraph-payload above. The neighbours navbar.js and navbar.css are not covered: they have fixed names and a byte-for-byte check, and stay refused. seed:ready reads the same declaration: deleting or renaming an owned-tree path is not a move of the layer, because a regen renames it anyway. readme-generated-regions — hunk by hunk . Directory READMEs mix authored prose with generated regions (<!-- kg:subgraph:begin --> … :end -->) whose file counts and listings change on every concurrent addition. A hunk inside a region takes the base’s side and the generator rewrites the region; a hunk in authored prose, or one that moves a region boundary, refuses. File-count churn is resolved here; the README keeps its exact counts. standalone-baseline — take the base, regenerate NOTHING . cat-harness-tools/scripts/standalone-baseline.json, check:standalone’s list of accepted standalone failures. It is the one take-base pattern with no regeneration, because it is a ratchet. Re-measuring after a merge would write any new standalone failure into the list unreviewed, which is exactly what the gate exists to stop. Git conflicts on it only when BOTH sides changed the list, so taking the base is fail-closed: if this side’s change was a new failure, its CI goes red until its author runs bun run standalone:baseline on purpose; if it was a fix, all that is lost is a shorter list, and the check reports it. beans — refused, by declaration . Before you go looking for the other session, check whether there is one. A beans/defs/** conflict has two causes and they need different handling: . | cause | how to tell | what to do | . | two sessions edited one work item | the default branch’s claim note names a branch that is not yours | a coordination question — talk to them | . | one session: the claim landed on the default branch, the completion stayed on the branch | the note names your own branch | no coordination needed; keep the completing value and the note | . The second is beans:claim’s normal path, not an edge case: it pushes the claim to the default branch so a sibling sees it before your PR exists, and your branch then edits the same work item to finish it. claim-bean.ts brings the claim COMMIT into the claiming branch after the push: a fast-forward when the branch has nothing of its own yet, otherwise a merge commit. The claim is then in the branch’s merge base, so finishing the work item merges cleanly (copying only the claim’s text still conflicts on updated_at, and a conflicted PR gets no CI at all). The conflict therefore means the claim could NOT be brought in: a detached checkout, local edits in the way, or a merge that would conflict. beans:claim says so (NOT in this branch's history) and falls back to the text mirror (mirrorClaimNote). Resolve the remainder by merging the default branch in, or by keeping the completing branch’s value and the note — and never by unioning the front matter, since a duplicated updated_at is check-bean-front-matter’s recorded defect. Work item definitions are authored work-plan state; two sessions editing one work item is a coordination question (bean-coordination). artefact-verification — refused, by declaration . scripts/artefact-verification.json, the per-check consumer-verification declaration. This is the entry that exists to stop a sweep, not to resolve one — and the one most likely to be globed by mistake, because it reads like a generated sidecar (under scripts/, a .json, its key set derived from package.json). Two facts, either one sufficient: . | task-io.ts classifies check:artefact-verification as TREE_READER, which has no outputs. No script writes the file, so regen has no writer to run and take-base is a silent discard rather than a resolution. | Its own _comment requires every none entry to carry a reason, in prose, and says the file “may only SHRINK”. A branch that adds a gated check adds an authored sentence — precisely what taking base would drop. | . So a conflict here is a genuine editorial merge: both reasons are wanted, and which survives is a judgement. Human merge is the cost of the file’s shape, not a hole in this catalogue. The falsifier: if a --write is ever added that composes the derived key set and carries existing reasons forward, the file becomes regenerable and this entry becomes take-base. Nothing today wants such a writer, and adding one to make merges cheaper would be building a mechanism to serve the merge tool rather than the gate. uploads — refused, by declaration . Uploaded source material: provenance-bearing input, never regenerated.

bb71d4634260.title: Adding a pattern
bb71d4634260.content: . | Measure first: replay recent merges with git merge-tree --write-tree and look at what the conflicting lines are, not just which files. | Add an entry with its why and the narrowest glob that covers it. Order matters: the first match decides. | Add a test that the unsafe neighbour is refused, not only that the case resolves. | Add a section here. | .

c8919ac13f8b.title: In CI — opt in with the merge-main label
c8919ac13f8b.content: .github/workflows/merge-main.yml, which lives in the folio-assistant index and not in this repository, is a second CALLER of the same command, never a second resolver. It runs main’s merge-base.ts --root on the PR’s branch (rule 3). It runs on a push to main, when the label is added, when a labelled PR is marked ready for review, and by hand: . | A sweep (a push to main, or a dispatch naming no PR) merges only a labelled PR that CONFLICTS with main. A PR that merges cleanly is skipped, because its pull_request CI already tests the merge ref (owner ruling 2026-11-05, branch-freshness). Adding the label, or a dispatch naming the PR, still merges a clean one. | Same-repository PRs only, and never a draft. A labelled draft is picked up when it is marked ready. | Runs queue; they are not cancelled in progress. For one PR, runs started by a push to main queue behind each other. A run of any other event (the label, ready-for-review, a dispatch) cancels an earlier run of the same event. Runs of different events can run at once, and the one that pushes second is rejected without overwriting anything. | It pushes only a proved merge, as a fast-forward of the branch it checked out; if the author pushed meanwhile the push is rejected and nothing is overwritten. | A refusal pushes nothing and lists the ✗ paths in its comment. Adding a pattern stays a person’s change, made here. It does NOT label the PR: a label asserting “a person is needed” outlives the condition that set it (merge-queue §”A hold has an EXPIRY and a trigger, or it outlives its reason”). The reason lives in the comment, which is dated and names the run. | A declared resolution that FAILS is a refusal too, not an unexplained red job. If taking the base or resolving a region throws, merge-base prints ` ✗ [: could not resolve] — <git's first error line>` and aborts, so the bot's comment names the path and the error. Staging a conflicted path uses `git add -f` in both resolvers (git exits 1 when staging an unmerged ignored path), safe because the path is one git listed as unmerged. `regen` reporting an unrepaired check is still a red job: that is a defect for a person to read, not a conflict. | One comment per PR, edited in place on every run — except a run that was cancelled (a newer label or ready-for-review run superseded it) or whose merge step reported no status, which leaves the comment untouched. The text is composed by cat-harness-tools/scripts/merge-main-comment.ts, which is unit-tested. | The merge commit is still judged by CI: pushed with the PUSH_BRANCH_TRIGGERING_CI credential (the harness GitHub App, or a repository secret of that name) when one is available, otherwise followed by a dispatch of code-quality-gates.yml on the branch, because a GITHUB_TOKEN push triggers no workflow. | . GitHub runs no pull_request CI on a conflicted PR, and main can move faster than an agent round. Use the label on a PR that is waiting on review rather than on its author; leave it off a branch somebody is pushing to.

f9295f77e97e.title: When a merge-train member is refused: bean, hand back, or dispatch
f9295f77e97e.content: A train is built in one of two ways, and they treat conflicts differently. The automated train (bun run cat merge:train, which merge-train.yml runs; the workflow is proposed in folio-assistant#2960) runs merge-base.ts --no-regen for each member, then one bun run cat regen, then one CI run. A conflict that a declared generated-path pattern covers is resolved at train time, and a conflict in a hand-written file refuses the member (owner ruling 2026-11-05, “Resolve generated only”; merge-queue §”The automated merge train”, proposed in cat-harness#1053). A steward’s hand train admits only members that stack with no conflict at all (merge-queue §”A train admits only members that STACK cleanly”), so it refuses a conflicted member before merging it. In either train, a member is also refused when the train’s combined result fails a gate that the member alone did not fail. The steward drops it and the train goes on without it. sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn executes what happens to the dropped member. The author’s side, the queue and the bounce-back are merge-queue; the hand-back format is the agent-handoff skill. A refusal has one of three causes: a conflict on a path refused by declaration (two PRs editing one work item, say), an authored or undeclared path, or a gate the combination fails that each member passed alone. Each refusal becomes a work item, because a PR comment or a chat message leaves nothing in the work plan to say it happened. 1. Open one bean per refused PR, and check before you create . beans create dedupes on nothing (see todo-manager §”Check before you create”). The title carries the PR number, so the check is exact: . beans list --json --search 'title:"Merge refused: #1822"' \ | jq -r '.[] | select(.title | startswith("Merge refused: #1822 ")) | select(.status != "completed" and .status != "scrapped") | .id' . | An open work item already exists for this PR: do not create a second one. Add the new refusal to it under ## Attempts with --body-append (never --body-file, which replaces the body). | Otherwise create one: type: bug, titled Merge refused: #<n> <first refused path or gate>. --parent and the create are one action (todo-manager §”After you create”). | . The parent is the epic or story the PR’s own work belongs to, not the steward’s epic. Find it in this order: the work item the PR’s branch adds or claims (git diff --name-only origin/main...<head> -- beans/defs/), then a work item id in the PR body or commit messages. Parent the refusal under that work item’s parent when the PR’s work item is a task, or under the PR’s work item itself when it is an epic or story. Then mark it --blocking <the PR's bean>. Only when the PR names no work item at all does it go under the steward’s own merge-gate epic, and the work item body says so. The body records what the owning session needs in order to act without asking: . PR #1822, head <sha> (the sha the train used), dropped from train `<train name>` (its other members, and the base sha it merged onto). ## Refused - `cat-harness/scripts/gen-library-jsonld.ts`: authored conflict, no declared pattern. Overlaps #1881, which is already in main. ## Done when - [ ] the PR's head merges main with `bun run cat merge:main` and no refusal, and CI is green on that head - [ ] the PR re-enters a train with a new `ready: <sha>`, and lands . For a combined-gate refusal, list the gate, its first failing line, and which other members the train held, because the fix may belong to either side. 2. Hand it back to the owning session, with a fail condition . The owning session is the one in the PR’s Claude-Session: trailer, or in its body. Hand the work item back to it in agent-handoff form: the steward is the coordinator and verifier, the owning session is the executor, and the owner rules on anything authored. The work item carries: . | ## Roles: steward (coordinator, verifier, closes), owning session (executor), owner (authored conflicts, any exception). | ## Report to: the PR. One line per event: <id>: started, <id>: done <sha>, <id>: blocked <why>. | ## Done when: as above. The verifier is the next train, not the executor’s own log. | ## Fails if, the fail condition, which is when the steward takes the work item back: . | no started line on the PR within 4 hours (these hours are as of 2026-10-08, when cat-harness was seeded; merge-manager-watcher acts at 2+ hours and merge-queue calls a PR stale after 24, and the owner decides which governs); | or no push to the PR branch within 24 hours; | or the owning session is gone: archived, failed, or unknown to get_session; | or the executor reports blocked on something it cannot settle. | . | . Send the hand-back to the session itself (send_message), as one line that names the work item and the branch, never the instructions. The instructions are in the work item, on the branch. After that, the steward does not edit the work item, except to add a further refusal (§1), record a dispatch (§3) or close it (§5). Anything else it learns goes to the PR (agent-handoff §1). The fail condition is a takeover, not a reminder, and that differs from agent-handoff §7 on purpose. There, the executor is in another environment and the coordinator cannot do the step, so an expiry only means asking again. Here, the work is in this repository and an agent can do it, so a missed deadline moves to §3. The one thing that is never done is putting a second writer on a branch whose first writer may still be live: before taking over, read the work item’s holder note and the PR’s last push (bean-coordination §”A quiet claim”). 3. When no live owner can be reached, dispatch one agent . If the owning session is gone, or the fail condition has fired, dispatch one agent on the PR’s branch (dispatch-agent). One agent is not a swarm; a second one is, and needs the owner’s per-swarm permission (swarm-management). Its budget is modest: one fix, one push, one report. | It may do what the patterns would have done had they been declared: bring main in with merge:main, regenerate, and fix a gate failure that has one mechanical answer. It pushes merge commits only, and never force-pushes. | It may not decide an authored conflict. Two sibling PRs editing one work item, one script changed differently on both sides, or a page over its budget only in combination: each of these is a choice between authors. The agent writes the question to the owner on the PR, with both sides quoted, the options and a default, and stops (interaction-modality §4.1). | It signs ready: only once it is the owning session. merge:guard takes the PR’s own session from the last session id in the PR body (signingSession in merge-guard.ts), and accepts a ready: <sha> marker only from that session. When the owning session is gone, the agent becomes the owner the way merge-queue §”Stalled for days” step 3 describes, with the owner’s go-ahead as there. It edits the body’s session line to its own session, records “taken over from . (gone)", and then marks the PR ready and signs. The steward never edits that line to itself, and never signs: while a Merge Manager is active, check 2 refuses a merging session that marked the PR ready itself. | The dispatch is recorded on the work item by the steward, before the agent starts: ## Attempts, with the date, the reason the fail condition fired, the agent’s session or task id, and the budget. | . Two failed attempts with the same cause go to the owner instead of a third dispatch (agent-handoff §7). 4. Comment on the PR once, and edit that comment . One comment per refused PR, edited in place as the work item moves on, as merge-main.yml does with its own comment. It names the work item, the head sha, the train, the refused paths, and who holds the fix (the owning session, a dispatched agent, or the owner). A second refusal of the same PR updates the same comment. Remove ready-to-merge (merge-queue). 5. Close the bean when the PR’s fate is settled . The steward is the verifier, so the steward closes: . | the PR lands: completed, with the merge commit as evidence; | the PR is closed unmerged: scrapped, with the reason and a link. The work item is never deleted (bean-coordination). | . A fix that is pushed but has not landed does not close the work item. The member must survive a train first. A refusal work item left open after its PR has gone is a stale hold.

26f066a30646.title: merge-conflict-patterns (skill)
26f066a30646.content: The skill merge-conflict-patterns as its source file cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/merge-conflict-patterns.md writes it, rendered by gen-processes-viz.ts because it has no instruction page on this site — do not edit here. All processes .

3a20f36db3c1.title: Merge manager watcher — the loop that runs the merge-steward role
3a20f36db3c1.content: Skill merge-manager-watcher: The merge manager agent’s watch loop: what wakes it, how often it looks, how it tells whether it is the active merge manager, what it reads each time, which process each reading sends it to (merge train, saturation meta-merge, stalled-agent takeover), and how it keeps the swarm in step with hold and done broadcasts. Use for “be the merge manager”, “watch the queue”, “who merges”, “the queue is stuck”, and when starting or handing over the merge-steward lane. Named by: Guideline Updates . The merge manager is the agent that holds the merge-steward role on one or more repositories (actor merge-manager). The role says what the steward may decide. The skills say how: what lands next (merge-queue), how it lands (merge-to-main), conflicts (merge-conflict-patterns), shared branches (ref-stewardship), and full runners (saturation-meta-merge). This page covers the loop that runs them: when to look, what to read, and where each reading leads. The process is sdlc/processes/merge-manager-watch.bpmn. It is one of two processes (owner ruling, 2026-11-07), split by phase so each fits a page: . | merge-request.bpmn, the sibling session’s side: find or elect the merge manager, send it the request, and handle a merge manager that stalls; | merge-manager-watch.bpmn, the merge steward’s loop on this page, with the owner lane below it for the batch card. The owner lane sits next to the only lane it talks to. | .

838a3caf63d6.title: Only the merge manager merges and re-pins (STRICT)
838a3caf63d6.content: Owner rulings, 2026-11-13: “they should not merge and only send to you to merge. I have not been initiating any merges”; “send to merge manager to handle merge and repin”; “send to you as merge manager to handle merge AND repin so you can handle trains and CI”. | Only the merge manager merges. No other session merges, enables auto-merge, pushes to main, or posts a ready: <sha> comment on another session’s PR. This holds in every repository. For a PR in a repository the merge manager cannot reach, the merge manager asks the owner by card; the PR’s session still does not merge it. | Sessions do not re-pin just in time. A PR that is green except for a re-pin, or for being behind its pins, goes to the merge manager as repin+merge: <owner/repo>#<n> <sha>, followed by the six lines (§”The merge request: six lines”). The merge manager makes the re-pin (its own PR, remote-mount §”Re-pinning”), sequences re-pin trains and CI, then merges. | A scheduled routine never merges. A routine or check-in that finds a green PR reports a ready: line to the merge manager, and does nothing else. | Standing re-pins and site repositories are the merge manager’s (owner cards, 2026-11-13: “C. No auto-merge”, replacing “A. MM dispatches, auto-merge OK”, and “A. Give MM access”). A standing re-pin run opens or updates its PR, labels it needs-repin, and never merges itself: the merge manager judges it once CI is green and merges it. The merge manager attaches each site repository and runs its re-pin: it dispatches the run, approves the held bot runs, and merges when green (remote-mount §”Standing consent”). | Held runs are approved by the merge manager. A re-pin commit pushed by a bot gets runs held at action_required, and the merge manager approves them before judging the PR. A held run executed nothing, so it is neither red nor green. | merge-guard becomes a required check (owner card, 2026-11-13, “A. merge-guard required status”). Once the tools layer’s workflow posts the merge-guard commit status (full tier, plus ready), the merge manager makes it a required status check on main in the layer repositories, through branch protection. Until then, merge-queue §”A PR lands only through merge:guard” holds as written. | A red index main pauses the re-pin train (owner card, 2026-11-13, “A. #3119, fix main, pause”). While the index repository’s main is red, the merge manager disables the re-pin train workflow, so no re-pin lands on a red base. It re-enables the workflow once main is green, and says so to the siblings and the owner both times. | A one-time consent is quoted where it acts. The owner’s card, with its date, goes in the re-pin PR’s body and in trust.consent’s evidence in index.config.json (remote-mount §”Trust”). | .

ef1d4d9a0fe3.title: The sibling’s side: find the merge manager first
ef1d4d9a0fe3.content: A coding agent whose PR is ready to merge does not know whether a merge manager exists. It checks, in this order: . | Is a merge manager active? Read the latest merge manager: <session id> announcement in the coordination group, then check that session is live: active, and it answered within the stall window (§”Liveness and stalls”). If so, send it the six-line merge request (below) and wait for its acknowledgement. | If none is active, elect one with the siblings by the fixed rule (§”Am I the active merge manager?”). A lone session is elected alone. The winner announces itself and takes the merge steward lane. Every other sibling notes the holder and sends it the request. Nobody merges while no merge manager holds the lane. | . An agent with no chat to the merge manager (a local agent such as agy, a GitHub Actions job, a scheduled routine, or any tool that only reaches GitHub) signals on its own PR with a label, because the PR is the message (merge-queue §”The PR is the message”; owner, 2026-11-13: “need a way to mark this for agents not able to communicate… label PR?”). It marks the PR ready for review and adds one of two labels: . | ready-to-merge: green; the merge manager merges it. | needs-repin: green except for a re-pin, or for being behind its pins; the merge manager re-pins, then merges. This is the label form of repin+merge:. | . A label is a request, never a merge: only the merge manager acts on either label (§”Only the merge manager merges and re-pins”). The agent puts the six lines in the PR body or a comment, and still asks the owner first (§”Ask the user before submitting” in merge-queue). Every sweep reads the open PRs carrying either label in the repositories the merge manager watches, and treats each as a request. One with no preview, or no six lines, goes back with a comment saying what is missing. Until the tools layer’s merge:guard accepts the label in place of a signed ready: <full head sha> comment (§”What this does not do yet”), the agent also posts that comment on its own PR. Where the announcement lives, so all can use it. The holder sends merge manager: <session id> to every sibling and the owner, and notes it durably on the coordination work item. A sibling started later reads the note, not anybody’s memory. A hand-over updates the note.

b8149b029e2c.title: When is a merge manager needed?
b8149b029e2c.content: This measure was first the condition for holding the lane at all (owner ruling, 2026-11-07: “merge manager needed if lots of conflicting CI runners causing merge slowdown”). Since 2026-11-13 it measures contention only (see below). The queue is contended while both of these hold: . | Two or more active sessions have ready PRs in the same repositories. | The merges are slowing each other down, which shows as either of: . | the runners are contended: more than about 10 queued runs on a repository (the pacing threshold in continual-progress §”Pace the ready marking”), or the oldest queued run is more than about 30 minutes old; | PRs keep conflicting with or superseding each other: duplicate re-pins, or rebases that invalidate each other’s CI. | . | . The lane does not lapse (owner ruling, 2026-11-13, which supersedes the lapse of 2026-11-07). A quiet queue does not hand merging back to each session: a merge manager always holds the lane, and only it merges. The measured condition above now says when the queue is contended. The merge manager then batches through trains and enforces runner relief, rather than landing each PR as it comes.

bcf7f0f07e99.title: Am I the active merge manager?
bcf7f0f07e99.content: Exactly one live session holds the lane on each repository. It holds the lane when the owner gave it the lane, when it was elected (below), or when it took the lane over from a stalled holder (stalled-agent-triage) and told the owner. On taking the lane, it announces merge manager: <session id> to every sibling and to the owner, so that every sibling knows where to send PRs. On handing it over, it says to whom. A memory that one existed yesterday does not count, either way. A lone session is its own merge manager (owner ruling, 2026-11-07: “if single, can merge manage self”). When a session is the only active one in its coordination group, it queues its own PRs and asks the owner directly, with the same six-line merge request and the same card per batch. It needs no election and no hand-off. As soon as a second sibling becomes active, the election rule applies. With no merge manager, the siblings elect one (owner ruling, 2026-11-07: “if no merge manager, siblings self-determine which will play that role”). No merge manager is active when none has announced itself, or when the last one has gone inactive. The owner does not have to appoint one. The rule is deterministic, so two sessions cannot both claim the lane: . | The active session that owns the P0 PR (the fix for a red main, or the re-pin chain) takes the lane. | With no P0 PR, the earliest-created active session in the coordination group takes it (the created_at of list_sessions). | With two P0 owners, the earlier-created of the two takes it. | . The elected session announces itself as above, and hands over explicitly when it stops. On 2026-11-07 the previous merge manager, merge-planning, went inactive without a hand-off, and the owner had to appoint one. Liveness and stalls . The merge manager, like any agent, may stall (owner ruling, 2026-11-07). So it has a liveness duty: it acknowledges each merge request within about 10 minutes of receiving it (the role’s holding.heartbeatMinutes; a request wakes it), and posts a heartbeat to the coordination group with each sweep. A sibling treats the lane as vacant when its request has no acknowledgement within about 30 minutes (holding.stalledAfterMinutes), or when the merge manager’s session is inactive. It then runs stalled-agent-triage: it tells the owner, and re-elects without the stalled session. The new holder announces itself, takes over the queue, and tells the owner. A stalled coding agent’s PR is handled the same way, from the other side: the merge manager runs stalled-agent-triage on it (§”Where each reading leads”). Siblings send merge requests here, and the owner approves here (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “Approvals”, B: “all siblings should communicate merge requests to you. i will approve here. you queue/prioritize”, and “all my approval is here, not in siblings”): . | There is one merge manager session. | A sibling never merges its own PR. When the PR is ready, the sibling sends the merge manager a merge request in the six-line format below. | The owner approves in the merge manager’s session, with one card per batch that names each PR. An approval the owner gives in a sibling’s session does not authorise a merge. | A pre-approved PR, one the owner said to “merge when green”, needs no second card. | The merge manager queues the PRs in priority order: . | P0: fixes for a red main, and the links of the re-pin chain; | P1: work those unblock; | P2: CI speed; | P3: everything else. | . | . The merge request: six lines . Owner ruling, 2026-11-07: “anything that indicated to merge should have link to PR, claude session, explanation of changes, preview URL”, and “put that in chat then ask to merge by card”. A sibling’s ready: message carries: . | the PR URL and the full 40-hex head SHA; | the claude.ai session URL; | an explanation of the changes, in 1-3 sentences; | the rendered preview URL for that head (feature-staging’s branches/ preview, or the layer’s equivalent), confirmed rendered, or no preview: <reason>; | what to look for in the preview; | the CI verdict on that head (owner ruling, 2026-11-13): full tier green as judged (rule 1 below). For a pin-only PR in a layer repository, line 6 reads pin-only: layer CI judges nothing (it mounts the root's lock), because its “No new failures” job runs no tests or gates and passes without judging anything. The evidence for those pins is the root’s own re-pin PR, not the layer’s green check. | . A PR that is green except for a re-pin is requested as repin+merge: <owner/repo>#<n> <sha> with the same six lines; line 6 then names what the re-pin must move. The merge manager re-pins it (§”Only the merge manager merges and re-pins”). The merge manager posts all six lines in its chat, then asks the owner by card. A request with no rendered preview and no reason goes back to the sibling.

e58ca3de3678.title: What wakes it
e58ca3de3678.content: . | A timer, at the sweep’s cadence (§”The sweep”): every 10-15 minutes while a P0 is in flight, every 30 minutes otherwise. This is a backstop, not the main signal. | A PR event on a subscribed PR: ready for review, CI finished, review submitted, merged or closed. Subscribe to every open non-draft PR in the repositories it holds. | A main run finishing, green or red. | A sibling’s message, for example “ready”, “hold”, or “done”. | . Never poll in a loop inside a turn. End the turn and let the next event wake it.

ca60af84da87.title: What it reads each time (live, never stored)
ca60af84da87.content: . | The open PRs: draft or ready, head SHA, mergeable state, owed checks, and whether any open decision is waiting on the owner. | The runner queue on each repository: queued and in-progress runs, and the age of the oldest queued run. | The latest main push run on each repository, and its verdict. | The owners of the PRs: the last push or comment by each owning session. | Every harness repository’s open main-red issue and its newest failed runs on main and gh-pages (§”Red mains and failing runs”). | .

1f9e94310416.title: Red mains and failing runs: dispatch a fixer
1f9e94310416.content: Owner, 2026-11-10: “That should be a part of merge manager (dispatch an agent to fix them)”, “Add to process”. A red main mails the owner on every push to it, so watching every harness repository’s main is part of the lane, not something a sibling notices by chance. What it watches. Every repository that runs the layer checks (the harness layers and the layers above them, and the index), whether or not the lane holds a PR there: . | the open main-red issue (kept by layer-main-qa.yml): its failing gates, tests and jobs; | the newest failed run on main, and on gh-pages for Pages deploys. | . Sort each failure into one cause before dispatching, because the fix lands in a different place for each: . | Cause | How to tell | Where the fix goes | . | Pins out of step | The failure names a file or test of ANOTHER layer, and that layer’s own main already differs (a test reads a page the newer layer removed; a heading or type the newer tools already have) | The next re-pin train on the index. A train that fails only on infrastructure gets its failed job re-run once | . | The layer’s own bug | The failure names this layer’s own file, and it fails at this layer’s own main | A fix PR in that layer, opened as a draft by the dispatched agent | . | A lower layer’s bug | The failure names a lower layer’s file, and it fails at that layer’s main too | A fix PR in the lower layer, then a re-pin | . | Infrastructure | “The runner has received a shutdown signal”, a Pages deploy stuck at syncing_files until it times out | Re-run once. A second failure is real: a Pages timeout goes to the site-size work | . Re-run policy (owner, card Q-RERUN-1 B, 2026-11-12). Every run of a PR emails the owner when it fails, and on 11-11 more than half of the failure emails came from re-runs. So a “re-run once” in the table above is bounded by these rules: . | Re-run a PR’s CI only when that PR is about to merge, which means it is approved (or non-content inside a merge window) and nothing else blocks it. | Never re-run held content or committee PRs (smart-ra CS- items, dth-* content, anything without an owner approval). | After a GitHub outage, wait until GitHub status reports healthy before re-running anything. Never re-run PRs in a batch. | Before re-running a re-pin PR, first refresh its pins to the current mains, so the lock-coherence gate does not fail again. | An update-branch also starts a run, so it follows the same rules. | . Dispatch. One fixer agent per cause, never one per repository: a single lower-layer bug can redden every layer above it. Give it the failing run, the cause row above and the repository, and have it open a draft fix PR, linked from the main-red issue. The fix is a P0 (§”Liveness and stalls”). Track it like any other PR in the lane, and close the loop when the next main run is green and the main-red issue closes. What it never does. It does not silence the failure: the report job stays red while main is red (owner, 2026-11-10, card “Merge #1812?”, B “Don’t merge”). It does not skip, disable or quarantine a gate or a test.

28f6bb11a5a5.title: The sweep
28f6bb11a5a5.content: Owner ruling, 2026-11-07 (card, about 07:55Z): the merge manager’s sweep is documented and tooled. Cadence. Every 10-15 minutes while a P0 PR (a fix for a red main, or a link of the re-pin chain) is in flight; every 30 minutes otherwise. A PR event, a merge request or a main run finishing may start a sweep early. One sweep, in this order: . | Run merge:watch over every repository the lane holds. It makes the four readings above, and judges each PR by every judge (rule 1 below): . bun run cat merge:watch -- --config merge-watch.json --json . Name the repositories with --repo <owner/name> (repeatable), --repos a,b,c, or --config <file.json> ({"repos": [...], "staleHours": 2}). --stale-hours <n> sets when a silent PR owner is flagged (default 2). The layers whose re-pins need the owner’s consent default to smart-* (the WHO SMART upstream layers; an entry ending in * matches a prefix). --exclude-layer <name> (repeatable) or a config’s excludedLayers replaces the default. Per repository it prints: . | each PR’s verdict, with a route flag: workflow changes go to a direct merge, a folio-assistant PR to the merge train, a pin on an excluded layer needs the owner’s consent, and superseded-by #N marks a duplicate; | the runner queue: queued and in-progress runs, the oldest queued run’s age, by event; | main’s latest push verdict; | each PR owner’s last push or comment, with stale owners flagged; | runner-relief candidates (§”Runner relief”). It only reports them, and never lists a main push run that has started. | . Its verdict is rule 1: every “No new failures” judge passes, each shard’s Q-PIPE-1 table lists 0 new failures, and any run queued or in progress on the head blocks. | Check each green request with bun run cat merge:request:check -- <file|-> (--json for machine output; exit 0 accepted, 1 refused, 2 could not determine). It parses the six lines, and checks that the SHA is the PR’s current head and that the preview was built for that head. Send a refused request back with the reason. Post each accepted request’s six lines in this chat. | Ask the owner with one batch card for all of them, in priority order. Leave off any PR in the pre-approval ledger (below). | Land what is approved. A workflow PR, or a PR in a repository with no train, merges through merge:guard. A folio-assistant PR that does not change .github/workflows/ gets the merge-train label (rule 8 below). | Send landed: <repo>#<n> <sha> to each session that was waiting, or back: <repo>#<n> <reason> for a PR that cannot land. | Post the heartbeat, and re-arm the timer at the cadence above. | . A helper may tabulate, never write. A helper agent may run step 1 and tabulate the result (rule 6 below). It never posts, labels, merges, comments, closes or pushes. Steps 2-6 are the merge manager’s. The pre-approval ledger. When the owner says “merge when green” for a named PR, the merge manager records it: the PR, the owner’s words, and when. It keeps the record on the coordination work item, beside the merge manager: note, so a successor inherits it. A PR in the ledger needs no second card. It lands at the first sweep that finds it green, and then leaves the ledger. The ledger covers only the PRs it names. A standing instruction to “merge everything green” is rule 2’s standing OK, not a ledger entry.

cad5beec3a9f.title: Where each reading leads
cad5beec3a9f.content: | Reading | Process | . | A merge request for a PR that is all green (rule 1 below) but not yet approved | Post its six lines in chat, then put it on the owner’s next batch card (§”The merge request: six lines”). A request with no rendered preview and no reason goes back | . | A repin+merge: request | Make the re-pin as its own PR, in a re-pin train with any others due, then land the requested PR on top of it (§”Only the merge manager merges and re-pins”) | . | An approved, all-green folio-assistant PR with no .github/workflows/ change | merge-train (Process_MergeTrain): add the merge-train label instead of merging it (rule 8 below) | . | An approved, all-green PR that changes .github/workflows/, or is in a repository with no train | Merge it directly through merge:guard. A workflow PR needs no approval beyond the batch card (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “Workflow PRs”, A) | . | Queued runs 60+ minutes old with nothing landed, or the owner says runners are full | First relieve the runners (§”Runner relief”). Then saturation-meta-merge: offer the card, never run without the owner’s tap | . | A PR whose owner has not pushed or answered for 2+ hours | stalled-agent-triage: tell the owner and take it over | . | main red, in any harness repository | §”Red mains and failing runs”: sort the cause, dispatch a fixer. The fix goes to main as its own PR first; when a dispatched post-merge-regen verify run says main is stale, a regen dispatched for the next PR commits the fix and that PR lands with priority (merge-queue §”Merge steward procedure: post-merge verification”). Trains wait for main to be green If it is the index repository’s main, disable the re-pin train until it is green (rule 7 of §”Only the merge manager merges and re-pins”) | . | Nothing to do | End the turn with no message | .

455cd7415a63.title: Merge-sweep rules (STRICT)
455cd7415a63.content: . | “All green” is exact. It has three parts. | Finished. Every check run on the head SHA has completed. Anything queued or in progress blocks. Wait for every tier, e2e included. A merge made before the last tier finished broke main (folio-assistant#2955). | Full tier. The “No new failures” judge, or every full test shard, ran. A draft or fast-tier-only pass never counts. | Green as judged, by every judge (owner ruling, 2026-11-07). Where a “No new failures” judge exists, its success is part of the verdict, but an aggregate job covers only the parts it names. folio-assistant’s “Repository gates (hard)” is one such job. Each bun test shard carries its own Q-PIPE-1 “no new failures” table, and each table must list 0 new failures. On 2026-11-06, folio-assistant#2985’s aggregate was green while 4 shards each reported a new failure. A red shard whose failures are all main’s known failures is fine when its table lists 0 new ones. With no judge, each check must have concluded success, skipped or neutral. | . A cancelled job counts only when a later run of the same workflow on the same head SHA passed the matching job (concurrency supersession). Merge with expectedHeadSha set to the full 40-hex head SHA, never a short one. | Standing OK. An owner instruction such as “merge everything green” is an explicit OK for every PR that meets rule 1, until the owner withdraws it. Merges still follow any stated chain order: a later PR in a chain waits for the earlier one. | One PR per fix. Before opening a fix or re-pin PR, search the open PRs in that repository for the same files. If one exists, compare the diffs and coordinate instead. If a duplicate is found later, the author of the later PR closes it, after checking that the diffs are identical. While main is red, one session owns the re-pin that fixes it, and says so to the merge-planning session. | A re-pin is a cross-layer set. Find every layer the change needs, a main-red fix or any other, and pin them together in one re-pin, to the current mains. Pins move only forward. Verify on a fresh mount (mount:remote --fresh). A stale container mount gives false local passes. The rules and an example are in remote-mount §”Re-pinning” (owner rulings, 2026-11-06, card “Pin target”, A, and 2026-11-07). | Hand back private caches. A PR that adds its own cache scheme instead of the shared cached-step is held, not merged, and goes back to its author. Cache-first CI, rule 1: every cache goes through cached-step. | Tabulation can be delegated. A helper agent may tabulate the sweep under these rules. The helper never touches the PRs the steward owns, and never pushes, comments or closes. | The train’s PRs are the train’s. A PR labelled merge-train or merge-train-batch is landed by the merge train only, in a batch with one main move and one main CI run. The sweep skips it, as merge-main.yml does; every other PR that meets rule 1 merges as before. A sweep that merges a labelled PR one at a time starves the train (owner ruling, 2026-11-06: “1. The train”). | Approved PRs go through the train (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “Train”, A). When the owner approves a folio-assistant PR that does not change .github/workflows/, the merge manager adds the merge-train label instead of merging it. The train lands a batch with one CI run. Merging one PR at a time cost about 6.7 runs per merged PR. A PR that changes workflows, and a PR in a repository with no train, merges directly. | Stacks merge bottom-up (owner ruling, 2026-11-07). A PR whose body says stacked on <repo>#<n> waits for that PR. The merge manager lands the base first, the stacked PR’s owner retargets it onto main and merges main in, and only then does it count as ready. A stacked folio-assistant PR gets the merge-train label only after it has been retargeted to main. A cross-layer stack waits until its pin names the dependency’s merge commit on main. The merge request lists the order, and the batch card keeps it. | A re-pin PR holds only pins (owner ruling, 2026-11-07: “keep repins on own PR so easier to stack dependencies”). When the sweep finds a re-pin PR (one that changes index.config.json or index.lock.json) that also carries a feature, workflow logic or a fix, the merge manager does not land it. It sends it back, and asks for the extra change to be split onto a PR stacked on the re-pin, or into the layer that owns the fix. Counter-example: folio-assistant#2985 carried #2999 and a caches:viz gate line inside its re-pin. Exception (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “A. Allow the exception”): a change mutually dependent with the re-pin, where neither passes alone, may share the PR when its body says why (as a content layer’s re-pin did on 2026-11-07). The merge manager checks the reason; a change that only needs the new pins still stacks. | .

0aafc565bb1b.title: Runner relief
0aafc565bb1b.content: The merge manager enforces the pacing rule of continual-progress §”Pace the ready marking” (owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “Cancel CI”). When the runners are saturated, it: . | closes superseded or duplicate PRs, such as a re-pin whose commits another open PR already carries, and cancels their runs; | cancels stale queued runs that never started, but never a main push run that has started; | asks the owners of P3 PRs to return them to draft. | .

73c297707649.title: Keeping the swarm in step
73c297707649.content: . | Hold. Before any batch landing (a train or a meta-merge), message every sibling that pushes to the repositories involved: what is about to land, and “hold pushes, merges and run cancels here until done”. | Done. After the landing, post “done” with what landed and what is still open. Post it even when the owner chose not to go ahead. A hold with no “done” is an outage. | Hand back. A PR that cannot land (conflict, protected path, red) goes back to its owner with the reason, on the PR’s own thread or work item. It is never fixed inside the train. | Report. After every landing, report to the owner: what merged, the main verdict on each repository, and any open decision. Keep it to one message. | .

510b1a66cf52.title: Safety rules (STRICT)
510b1a66cf52.content: These come from the role; the watcher is the step that acts on them: . | Only the merge manager merges, in any repository, and a scheduled routine never merges (§”Only the merge manager merges and re-pins”). | Merges happen only on the owner’s explicit OK, given in the merge manager’s session. A tap on the batch card counts, and the card names each PR. A standing OK counts for the PRs it covers (rule 2). A sibling’s or coordinator’s request does not count, and neither does an approval the owner gave in a sibling’s session. | Never merge committee content, change sets (CS-), or held subscriptions/ trees. Never touch WHO or smart-* upstream repositories. | Never push .github/workflows/ changes without the workflows permission. | Never cancel a main push run that has already started. | Never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get to green. | .

92baa12967f3.title: What this does not do yet
92baa12967f3.content: . | merge:guard check 3 (ready-marker) still asks for a ready: <sha> comment signed by the PR’s own session. That still works: a session may post the marker on its own PR, and then sends the six lines to the merge manager. What it cannot cover is a PR whose session can neither post nor reach GitHub, because nobody else may post the marker for it (rule 1). Follow-up for the tools layer (owner, 2026-11-13: “update process and tools”): . | check 3 accepts the ready-to-merge label, alone or with a pinned head, in place of the ready: comment, so sessions stop posting ready comments; | merge:watch lists the PRs labelled ready-to-merge and needs-repin as the merge manager’s queue, each with its CI verdict; | every merge path (merge:guard --merge) says that only the merge manager runs it, and a standing re-pin run opens a needs-repin PR and never merges (card “C. No auto-merge”); | a workflow posts the merge-guard status, so that it can be required on main (card “A. merge-guard required status”); | --no-merge-manager is renamed to say what it now means: the merge manager landing a PR of its own. | . | The needs-repin label must exist in each repository the merge manager watches before an agent can use it. | The timer is each session’s own scheduled check-in. No workflow wakes the merge manager yet. | .

a3d2a5477ff1.title: merge-manager-watcher (skill)
a3d2a5477ff1.content: The skill merge-manager-watcher as its source file cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/merge-manager-watcher.md writes it, rendered by gen-processes-viz.ts because it has no instruction page on this site — do not edit here. All processes .

eda1a85b723b.title: Merge queue — what lands next, and as what
eda1a85b723b.content: Skill merge-queue: Order the ready PRs and land them as a train: read each PR’s live facts, let the reprioritisation table place it, merge the members together, run the gate set on the combination, and on red attribute and eject the culprit rather than reject the train. Every merge goes through merge:guard. Use for “merge the ready PRs”, “land this PR”, “what lands next”, “run a merge train”, “why was my PR ejected”, “move this PR up”, and when tuning the train’s order or size. Named by: Guideline Updates . sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn is the process. The ORDER is computed by sdlc/processes/decisions/merge-priority.dmn; the facts it reads are derived by scripts/merge-queue.ts; what the steward decided is recorded against schemas/sdlc/merge-queue.ts. This page says what each piece is FOR.

cc209214572a.title: The rule everything else follows from
cc209214572a.content: The queue stores decisions, never GitHub’s facts. CI status, mergeability, labels and head SHA change without the queue being told, so a stored copy is stale the moment it is written and a reader cannot tell which. They are read live at each step. What a queue entry holds is what the steward DECIDED — the placement, a hold, an ejection — with who decided it, when, and the evidence URL it acted on. FORBIDDEN_FACT_KEYS in the schema refuses an entry that carries a fact.

9f7dfe738d64.title: Handing a PR to the queue — the sibling session’s side (STRICT)
9f7dfe738d64.content: merge-train.bpmn has two lanes that matter here: . | sibling-session (“Sibling session”): whoever submits a PR to the queue and fixes it when it is handed back. | merge-steward (“Merge steward”): whoever orders and lands the queue. | . Both are ROLES, not sessions, so nothing in this section depends on which session holds either lane. The PR is the message . The steward reads open PRs labelled ready-to-merge, and nothing else. A comment posted anywhere else reaches nobody: not on a PR you believe is the steward’s, and not on an issue. A session that cannot message the merge manager labels its own PR instead: ready-to-merge when it is green, needs-repin when it is green except for a re-pin. Only the merge manager acts on either label (merge-manager-watcher §”The sibling’s side: find the merge manager first”; owner, 2026-11-13). Ask the user before submitting . When you finish your work and are ready to merge, ask the user before submitting to the merge queue. Do not apply ready-to-merge or post the ready: marker autonomously without asking the user if you should submit. Submitting to the queue requests landing the code on main; the user or owner confirms the submission. While a merge manager is active, tell it, and never merge yourself . Owner ruling, 2026-11-07, card “Approvals”, B: siblings send merge requests to the merge manager, and the owner approves only in the merge manager’s session. So, besides the steps below, send the merge manager the six-line merge request: the PR URL and full head SHA, your session URL, what changed, the rendered preview URL (or no preview: <reason>), what to look for in it, and full tier green as judged. A request with no preview and no reason comes back. Never merge your own PR. An approval the owner gives in your session does not authorise a merge. The merge manager posts your request in its chat, asks the owner on its batch card, and orders the queue: merge-manager-watcher §”Am I the active merge manager?” and §”The merge request: six lines”. Find the merge manager before you send: the latest merge manager: <session id> announcement, noted on the coordination work item, names a session that must also be live. When none is active the siblings elect one by a fixed rule; a lone session is elected alone; the lane never lapses into self-merging (owner ruling, 2026-11-13); and one that does not acknowledge within the stall window is treated as stalled (merge-manager-watcher §”The sibling’s side: find the merge manager first”). Submitting to the queue . To submit, do all of these on YOUR PR: . | Owed CI is green on the head, for a release. See §”Admission asks which runs are OWED”. On a non-release merge CI is advisory (owner, card Q-CIB-4 A, 2026-11-08): it is read and reported, and it does not hold the PR (merge-to-main §”CI gates a release only”). | The PR is ready for review, not a draft. | It carries the label ready-to-merge. | It has a comment ready: <full head sha>, signed with your session link (https://claude.ai/code/session_…). Every session acts with the owner’s token, so the link is the only thing that tells sessions apart. A _Generated by Claude Code_ footer alone is not a signature. | It does not carry needs-merge-human. merge-main.yml adds that label when it refuses a merge and never removes it. If you have since merged main by hand, remove the label, and say why in a comment. | The body has no unticked box, and there is no open question to the owner or the steward. | An agent-touched PR has an adversarial review on its head, recorded on the merge-reviews state branch by a session that is not the author (adversarial-code-review). The gate is warn-only for now, so a missing verdict is reported, not refused. A train keeps each PR’s verdict, because the review is per head. | . Watch status after submitting — never fire-and-forget . When you submit something to the merge queue, you need to watch what its status is. Submitting is not the end of your turn. Watch the GitHub Actions runs on the head (check:head-has-run), evaluate merge-guard, and monitor whether the PR is admitted into a train or whether it is refused, held, or failing checks. If CI fails, diagnose and repair the failure immediately rather than leaving a failing PR in the queue. Merge order goes on the PR, and setting an order is the owner’s call. | Write it in the ready: comment, on every PR it concerns (“merge before #N”). | Quote the owner’s ruling with its date. | When two PRs must not land in the wrong order, keep the label OFF the later one until the earlier one lands. A label is the only hold the steward is certain to see. | . After submitting: do not spend CI you do not need yet . Once CI has confirmed the PR, a submitter far back in the queue should not burn CI cycles keeping up with a churning main. Every merge of main into your PR re-runs the whole suite. While other PRs are landing, each of those runs is obsolete before the steward reaches you. | The first green is what admits you. Your ready: marker stays valid across merge-main bot merges (see “A push makes the marker stale” below), so the steward can still see a PR that is a few merges behind. | Far back, stand still. If your PR is not in the next train or two (the steward’s status comment on your PR gives your position), do not merge main by hand to stay current. Take merge-main off as well: that label makes the bot merge main into your PR on every push to main (§”Your merge cadence is an input to the bot’s throughput”). | Near the front, catch up once. When you are in the next train, or the steward asks you to: . | put merge-main back on, or merge main by hand (prepare-merge §”Submodules: check the pointers BEFORE you stage the merge”); | let CI go green; | post a fresh signed ready:. | . | A conflict is the exception. If main now conflicts with your PR, fix it when you see it, wherever you are in the queue. A conflict is work, not churn. | . A push makes the marker stale. A head newer than your ready: sha is not intake, unless every commit since is a merge-main bot merge. Post ready: again for the new head once CI is green on it. Do not post “ready soon”: it is not intake, and it costs the steward a read. The steward’s side: reach a submitter who has fallen behind . While watching the queue, and after every reshuffle or disentangling of trains, the steward checks the PRs near the front. A PR there can be: . | behind main and conflicted; | red, or with an owed run missing on its head; | carrying a stale ready:; | carrying needs-merge-human. | . When the steward finds one, it tells the submitter. It never fixes the PR on the submitter’s behalf, and never waits in silence. It uses the skills it already has: . | The status comment on the PR, edited in place. It states the position, what is missing, and by when. Its shape is the one in merge-conflict-patterns §”When a merge-train member is refused”. | A hand-back work item when the PR is ejected or handed back (same section). The submitting role picks it up even if the original session is gone. Every hand-back gets one, not only a train ejection. That covers Rule_Refused, Rule_HeadNotGreen, Rule_NotReady, and a merge:guard refusal on a PR the owner asked to land. A PR comment and a queue entry are not a hand-back on their own: the work plan cannot see them. | Shape: titled Merge refused: #<n> <cause>, type: bug, parented under the PR’s work item’s parent (or under the PR’s work item when it is an epic or feature), marked --blocking that work item. | Body: the refused checks, roles, the brief (link the takeover plan if there is one), where to report, Done when, and Fails if. | Dedupe: check first, because beans create dedupes on nothing. | Process: run it through sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn (workflow_start), not from memory. | . merge:steward prints ✗ handed back with NO open hand-back bean: #… and carries handBackBean per PR in --json, because a procedure that lives in another skill is skipped unless something checks for it. | A direct message as the fast path, by the recipe below. Use it when the PR is next and waiting costs a train. | The queue entry records the hold or ejection, with its reason and expiry (§”The steward answers in the queue”). | . A submitter told “you are next” catches up at once. That is the trade this section makes: CI is spent on the PRs about to land, not on the whole queue. Address the ROLE, never a session . The Merge Steward is a lane in merge-train.bpmn, not a particular session, and whoever holds it today may not hold it tomorrow. So the handover must not depend on who that is: . | no session id written anywhere, since it dies with its container; | no “they are active on PR #N”, since that PR may merge or the role may move; | no message as the channel. | . Whoever takes the lane next reads the same open PRs and the same queue entries. A direct message is a fast path on top of that, never a replacement. Use one when it is the more efficient tool, and say how you used it. It saves the receiver a polling cycle, but it never counts as handing over: the PR’s own state still has to say ready. The same recipe works in both directions: . | Find whoever holds the other role now. Do not use a remembered session id. | Cloud: run list_sessions (claude-code-remote). Match the session whose title or external_metadata.current_branches shows the lane, or the PR’s head branch when you are looking for a submitter. | Same machine: run ListAgents. | . | Check it can receive. For a cloud session, run get_session(id) and confirm cross_session_inbound == "available". | Send one line. Use send_message (cloud) or SendMessage (same machine), naming the PR and the head sha. The PR comment stays the record; the message only points at it. | If any step fails, stop. Do not post the message as a comment on some other PR or issue instead. | . coordinate §”What actually reaches a sibling” has the measurements of which tool reaches which kind of session. The steward answers in the queue, and the queue lives on the beans branch . Once the steward has decided something about your PR (a placement, a hold, an ejection), that decision is an entry under beans/queue/<pr>.json. The entry carries pr and beans, the work items and epics the PR serves; name them in your PR body so the steward can copy them. That list is the association between a PR and its work items. Where to read it depends on the state-branch cutover. The queue is moving to its OWN branch, cat/cat-harness/merge-queue — §”Where the queue is GOING” below — and where the two disagree, that section governs: . | Before the cutover, main is authoritative. Entries reach it only through the steward’s own PRs, a PR cycle late, so the edited-in-place status comment on your PR is the live answer. | After the cutover, beans/ (with queue/ inside it) is authoritative on the orphan branch cat/cat-harness/beans. Read it with bun run cat state:mount. The steward writes an entry the moment it decides, then bun run cat state:push, which splices only the changed paths onto the tip and stops on a conflicting write instead of overwriting it. The entry is then live for everyone, and the status comment is a courtesy that points at it. | . The branch’s manifest.json says which state it is in ("authoritative"). Read that rather than this paragraph. The cutover also changes what a work item can do here. A work item created on a code branch is invisible until the PR lands; a work item written through state:push is visible at once. A submitter can then note on the PR’s work item that it is submitted, and the steward can answer on the same work item. The PR state above stays the intake signal either way: the work item is where the conversation is kept. Not GitHub’s merge queue. It is not offered on a personal-account repository. The merge guard (bun run cat merge:guard <pr>) checks the six submission points mechanically; run it against your own PR before you announce.

1a5aeb69d885.title: Where the queue is GOING, and the tool that will write it
1a5aeb69d885.content: Not cut over yet. The queue is still on main under beans/queue/. The store and CLI below exist; the cutover to its own branch, cat/cat-harness/merge-queue, is a separate small change during which the steward pauses queue writes. Until it lands, merge:queue:read reads the checkout and merge:queue:record refuses — keep committing entries to main as §”The steward answers in the queue” describes. The branch’s manifest.json says which state it is in. Why the queue comes off main at all is structural: an entry on main arrives only through a pull request, and the steward does no development work — it must not open PRs of its own, which would have it setting its own priority in the queue it manages, spending the CI the queue is starved of, and judging its own head. On main, the one actor whose decisions the queue records is the one actor that cannot write to it. After the cutover: . bun run cat state:mount # the queue on disk at its declared path bun run cat merge:queue:read # the recorded decisions bun run cat merge:queue:record --pr <n> --class <c> --rank <r> --rule <id> \ --reason "<why>" --by <your session URL> # ...or --position <n> for an owner override . | record pushes by default, as a splice onto the branch tip carrying the blob each file was read at. So the entry is live for every sibling at once, and a steward who edited the same entry since gets this write stopped as a conflict with the path named rather than overwritten. On a conflict, re-mount and decide again; nothing was pushed and the local edit is the only copy. --no-push leaves it in the mount, where nobody else can see it. | --reason and --by are required. A placement nobody can explain cannot be honoured or safely undone by the next steward, and every session here acts with the owner’s token, so the session link is the only thing that says which steward decided. | An unreachable queue is not an empty one. merge:queue:read exits 4 and readQueueEntries THROWS when the branch is not mounted, because “no decisions recorded, all clear” printed over a graph nobody read is a false clean. Exit 1 — declared-but-absent — is a different answer with a different remedy. | The decisions are read back. merge:steward feeds recorded overrides into the table’s ownerOverride input and their positions into the order, treats an un-cleared ejection as refused, and prints a live hold, because a decision nobody reads back is a decision nobody took. | . The queue’s decisions and a finished train run’s evidence (under workflows/) live in different stores, one state:mount apart. The trade is deliberate: kept together on main, the queue could hold no entry the steward wrote.

a6390bc5c343.title: Placement is computed, not chosen
a6390bc5c343.content: GW_Placement is DMN-backed, so workflow_complete refuses a hand-supplied outcome there. The table (hit policy FIRST) answers a route (admit or hand back), a class (PRIORITY_CLASSES), a rank and whether the PR rides alone. | An owner override is an INPUT (ownerOverride), never an outcome. The owner places a PR by hand in Task_Override; the schema refuses an override placement without a reason. | Independence is decided on AUTHORED paths (authoredPaths, touchesShared). Generated paths are excluded because merge-conflict-patterns already resolves them; counting them would make every pair of PRs conflict. | Ties go to the oldest PR (orderQueue): overrides at their positions, then rank, then PR number. | .

9228dd7bad08.title: Admission asks which runs are OWED, never whether anything is red
9228dd7bad08.content: On a release, a member is admitted on ownCi == "green" (on a non-release merge ownCi is reported, not required; owner, card Q-CIB-4 A, 2026-11-08), and green means every workflow owed for the head’s event ran and succeeded. It does not mean “nothing is failing”. A head can have every expected job name present, no failure anywhere, and still have runs in_progress and suites completed with conclusion: action_required that executed nothing. Counting the runs does not catch it. Only asking which runs are owed for this event catches it, and check-head-has-run is the one thing here that asks. Do not write a second checker: it already keeps the states apart, has a test, and is already wired into pr-checks-present.bpmn. Its five states are the five values of ownCi, and collapsing any two is the defect: . | value | means | . | green | every owed run present and successful — the only admitting value | . | red | an owed run ran and failed | . | missing-required | it HAS runs, but not the ones owed | . | none | GitHub answered and nothing names this head | . | unknown | could not ask: no network, rate limit, HTTP error | . unknown is handed back, never admitted and never reported as red: telling somebody their head is unverified when you merely could not look trains them to ignore the signal, which costs more than the gap. This is a gate, not advice. Rule_HeadNotGreen in merge-priority.dmn sits immediately after Rule_Refused under hitPolicy="FIRST", so anything but green routes to hand-back before any admitting rule can fire, and workflow_gate refuses a hand-supplied outcome. A dispatch is not an owed run. workflow_dispatch is the designed workaround for the bot-actor push condition (merge-main.yml dispatches the gating workflows for exactly that reason), but a dispatched run is evidence about the TREE, not evidence that the owed pull_request run exists. Report the two facts separately.

4c155b1ab9a2.title: Overlap has a KIND, and a train is the right answer to one of the four
4c155b1ab9a2.content: conflictRisk answers is there a collision. A steward needs is it the kind a train is for, which is overlapKind: . | kind | means | what it needs | . | none | no path shared with any live member | nothing | . | generated-only | shares paths, every one resolved by a declared pattern | regeneration | . | shared-declaration | the only authored paths shared are shared declarations | ordering | . | authored | shares an authored path that is not a declaration | a train | . Four values rather than three because a shared declaration is a subset of an authored path, not a sibling: classify("package.json").strategy is refuse, so it is authored, and isSharedDeclaration("package.json") is true. A three-value partition would file a declaration-only collision under authored and build trains nobody needed. authored outranks shared-declaration, which outranks generated-only, because at each step the earlier kind is the one the later kind’s remedy cannot resolve. The partition is tested in scripts/tests/merge-queue.test.ts — including that a refused member cannot be the other side of a collision, since it never enters a train.

782a0db28b28.title: A train admits only members that STACK cleanly (STRICT)
782a0db28b28.content: A train is a stack: member n+1 merges onto main + members 1…n with no conflict at all, generated paths included, and with no semantic break (tsc and the gate set pass on the stack). Check every candidate before admitting it: . c=origin/main for p in <members in order>; do t=$(git merge-tree --write-tree $c pr/$p) || { echo "#$p does not stack"; break; } c=$(git commit-tree $t -p $c -p pr/$p -m stack) done . A member that does not stack is not admitted. It does not go in on the promise that merge:main will resolve it. It goes back to its own session, which merges main on its own branch, gets CI green, and re-signals.
