It does not prove a given sheet has the script installed or current: that is How to tell it works. Change the template, the builder or this table only together with that test. Rewrite the Config tab when the review anchors change, the draft link moves, or a tab or a header the script reads is renamed. Re-paste Code.gs only when the script itself changes. Renaming a header the script reads, without rewriting Config, leaves that column unlinked; it fails nothing.

0782dfb0e8f4.title: Ready for agent: Yes, No, Completed
0782dfb0e8f4.content: The script sets Ready for agent from Yes to Completed once the agent’s last push is later than the time Yes was set and the preview of it is live and current (no ⚠ in Staging review). An Editor sets Yes again to send the row back to the agent. A row that turns stale goes back to No from Yes or Completed. The agent never writes the Orange columns. Every pass ends with a finish stamp after the Ready time: . | The agent ends EVERY pass with a stamp from the tool: push --head <sha> when it committed, else done, which writes Agent completed and the step idle together. A proposal that waits for the Editor ends with step proposed. The script counts a later idle or proposed step as the end of the pass, the same as Agent completed. | Before stopping, the agent re-reads Ready for agent: if it was set after the pass began, the pass is not over; act on it (or done if there is nothing new). | A Ready for agent with no step recorded after it for 20 minutes shows “⚠ no agent has picked this up for N min: ask in the project chat” on the ⏳ line and in Agentic status, so a row with no agent never looks like quiet work. | Every log needs a watcher: the setup is not complete until an agent thread is watching the sheet. A thread acts only when something wakes it, so the watcher needs a scheduled wake: an hourly scheduled task, plus a chain of 3-minute delayed wakes (send_later) that each pass renews. Each wake runs the mechanical check of skill review-log-watch first, and does agent work only when it reports a change. For that check the script writes, in a drafting sheet, a hash of every cell people set on Contributor Feedback to the hidden Watch tab (F1:I1: Cells hash, the hash, Checked (UTC), the time), on every refresh and timer tick. In a public-comment sheet it covers Review Change Sets (Title, TWG (CS), every Committee Feedback column, Ready for agent, Dispositions confirmed, Ready for merge, Change Set (human)) and Review Public Comments (every Committee Feedback column, Disposition, Change Set (human), TWG (human)), keyed by Change-set id and comment No., so an inserted row changes nothing; it is written on every refresh, which the timer runs only when an edit or the Agent tab changed. Without a watcher, a Ready for agent waits until somebody happens to ask. | .

1297c6249cc8.title: One agent column, status on top
1297c6249cc8.content: A sheet without an Agentic status column gets the status on top of the agent column (Change Set Feedback (agent) or Feedback (agent)) instead: . ⏳ smart-ra#185 open, updated 2026-10-31 15:26Z; preview current (built 15:19Z). ↳ smart-ra#185 (PR open, 2026-10-31 15:26Z) · DPI-F at first use <the agent's proposal and any Decision needed question> . The ⏳ line and each ↳ line (one per pull request, linked; and the ask when people must answer) are the script’s; it replaces them on every refresh and never stacks them. The agent writes only what is below them and never starts its own text with ⏳ or ↳. Agentic status (filter) stays, for the filter views. A sheet that keeps its Agentic status column keeps the status there; delete that column to switch.

72683182c001.title: The QA gate, before Ready for merge
72683182c001.content: Who. A reviewer that did not write the change: another agent session, or a person. The authoring agent never gates its own pull request. What it checks, against the PR’s head commit: . | every comment (drafting: every feedback item) of the change set has one disposition (the script’s dispositionProblems already flags gaps); | each disposition agrees with the people’s Blue Disposition, where one is set; | each Accepted or Partially accepted item has its change in the PR’s diff, and the change does what the line says; | a Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate or Out of scope item has no change in the diff that contradicts it; | the diff changes nothing that no disposition accounts for; | the staging QA report for that commit has no failing gate. | . What it writes, on the Agent tab’s change-set row and nowhere else: . | QA gate (change set): first line Passed <head sha>: <one line> or Failed <head sha>: <the first problem>, then one line per problem; | QA report (change set): the link to the QA report for the staged commit: the tree pr/<n>/<sha> on the folio’s QA reports branch (in smart-ra, cat/cat-harness/qa-reports; check the branch name, it varies). | . When the gate passes, run agent-record.ts qa-pass (§”Writing the Agent tab with the tool”). What the sheet shows. Staging review reads review · QA report (both links), then the gate: ✓ QA gate passed (b20534f), or in bold ⚠ QA gate: no independent review yet: not ready for merge, ⚠ QA gate failed: <why>, or ⚠ QA gate stale: reviewed 1234567, PR now at b20534f: not ready for merge once the PR moves on (qaGate). If Ready for merge is set before the gate passes, the agent’s ⏳ line says it will not merge until it does, and the agent does not merge. A failed gate sends the change set back to the author, who updates the PR and its dispositions; the gate then runs again on the new head.

32ba1017dba4.title: Unconfirmed dispositions block the merge
32ba1017dba4.content: The agent’s disposition for a comment is a proposal until the committee records its own word in the people’s Disposition column. While any comment of a change set is still Pending (or empty) there, Disposition (agent) shows “⚠ Not confirmed by the committee (Disposition still Pending): Nos. …”. Staging review shows “⚠ dispositions not complete or not confirmed: not ready for merge”, and the ⏳ line says the agent will not merge until every disposition is complete and confirmed. The agent never merges such a change set, even with Ready for merge = Yes. agent-record.ts dispositions does not stop on this line, because confirming is the committee’s step, not a fault in the agent’s record. An Editor confirms in the Orange Dispositions confirmed column, left of Ready for merge. There are only three ways to confirm, and no per-comment checkbox: . | Yes confirms every agent disposition in the change set; | comment numbers typed in the cell (“No. 327”) confirm just those; a number outside the change set is flagged; | to differ on one comment, the committee sets that comment’s own Disposition on Review Public Comments, and a mismatch is flagged. | . The script adds the column itself, inside its locked run (so no other refresh writes by a shifted position), and keeps its Yes/No dropdown.

fb318b87f03b.title: Where the agent is: Agent step
fb318b87f03b.content: At every move the agent writes Agent step (change set) on its change-set tab, with agent-record.ts step <name> so the time comes from the clock. The script shows it on the ⏳ line for as long as it holds, e.g. “⏳ Agent: editing the document (since today 17:20Z)” (or “yesterday …”, or “3 days ago, 2026-10-28 …”), and adds “⚠ no update for N min” after 30 minutes. A question for a person (“Needs you: answer the Decision needed below, then set Ready for agent to Yes”) always comes first. The script adds the column, at the end of the tab, inside its locked run. | step | when the agent writes it | BPMN task | . | reading | it starts on new feedback or a Ready for agent | (start of Task_Propose / Task_EditInPullRequest; public comment: Task_AuthorEdits) | . | proposing | it writes or rewrites its proposal | Task_Propose (public comment: Task_ProposeChangeSets) | . | editing | it edits the document on the branch | Task_EditInPullRequest (Task_AuthorEdits) | . | pushing | it commits and pushes | end of the edit task, with push | . | staging | the preview is building | the staging step of the edit task | . | deploying | Pages is publishing the preview | as above | . | qa-review | it waits for the independent reviewer | Task_QaGate | . | merging | it merges after Ready for merge | Task_Merge (Task_Incorporate) | . | proposed | it has written a proposal and waits for Ready for agent = Yes; the ⏳ line says “Proposal ready: set Ready for agent to Yes” | end of Task_Propose | . | idle | it stops: done, or waiting on a person | — | . The agent writes its proposal straight into the feedback cell, which drops the ⏳ line; the timer watches that column (without the script’s own lines), so the status comes back on the next tick without anyone pressing Refresh. Write idle (or the next step) before leaving a change set; a step left behind turns into the “no update” warning.

78f72e6b1910.title: Rows at most 10 lines high
78f72e6b1910.content: Sheets cannot scroll inside a cell, so on the people’s tabs (Review Public Comments, Review Change Sets, Contributor Feedback) a row whose text would run past about 10 lines is fixed at that height and the rest is clipped. Clicking the cell shows the whole text in the formula bar, and double-clicking opens it scrollable. Rows that fit size themselves, and a row that shrinks back under the cap is released. The script estimates lines from column widths (capRows), so it needs no layout access.

b9e26ac01ef1.title: Structured cells and column hover text
b9e26ac01ef1.content: A list is never run together with semicolons. Agents write “What changed” and “What the PRs changed (change set)” one item per line, as • <item> (No. n), under a label line ending in a colon. The script splits any remaining a; b; c into bullet lines, and bolds line-start labels (What changed:, Proposed direction:) and comment references (No. 326, Nos. 1, 2 and 5). Every column head carries a hover note saying what the column holds and who fills it in, without naming its colour. The notes are HEADER_NOTES in the script, keyed by header (or <tab kind>|<header> where one header means different things on different tabs); a head named Name (initials) uses its Name (*) entry. The script owns the note on every head it knows and writes only notes that changed; a head it does not know keeps its own. A new column gets its note in the same change that adds its header; review-sheet.test.ts checks that every known head has one and that none names a colour. The QA report link opens the viewer, the preview review page’s per-section QA table (<review page>#heat), with the raw qa-reports entry beside it as “files”. Text in a cell that is not a link is written plain, so it never inherits a link’s blue underline.

2272a2a6ad7b.title: Sheet conventions (any agent-written Google Sheet)
2272a2a6ad7b.content: These hold for every Google Sheet an agent writes or keeps current, not only the review sheets: . | colour | who controls it | lock | . | grey | mechanical: ids, headers, copied source text | owner only | . | blue | people: the human-controlled columns | open to the sheet’s editors | . | orange | editor gates (Ready for agent, Ready for merge) | its own lock, owner plus the named editors | . | green | agent-derived: links, joins, status | owner only | . | Templates are locked to the owner except the blue columns; the orange gates carry their own lock that starts with the owner alone. | The Config tab is visible, never hidden, and locked to the owner: the agent writes it, people can read what the sheet is set up for. | Instructions name no colour. The key on the first line reads “Column colours:” then one phrase per colour (“your input, by …”, “written by the agent”, …), each shown in its colour, and the steps name columns (“Reviewers update Contributor Feedback”, “an Editor sets Ready for agent”), never a colour. The script’s colourInstructions shows each column name bold in a darker shade of that column’s header fill, on every refresh, so text the agent rewrites through the API, which drops the colours, gets them back within a minute. | Which template depends on the document’s authoring stage: the Contributor template while it is being drafted and authored, the Public Comment Review template once public comment opens. | .

21e3adbc4b73.title: Archiving the log
21e3adbc4b73.content: Every review log keeps a copy in its document’s knowledge graph, beside the comments and change-sets it reviews (issue #682; owner, 2026-11-08): . | File | What | . | review/public-comment/logs/<log-id>.json | the log’s review-log/1.0.0 node: sheet id and link, document, role (master or contributor), each tab’s header row and the role of each column, read from its header colour (blue = human, orange = editor, green = agent, grey = script), the workbook’s SHA-256 | . | review/public-comment/logs/<log-id>.xlsx | the log as a workbook: values and their types, hyperlinks, notes, fills, a frozen header row | . The workbook is .xlsx, so a person opens it in Excel, Google Sheets, Numbers or LibreOffice. It is never a custom JSON. There is one workbook per log, and it is overwritten, never added to as a dated copy. Git history is the history, and each commit message lists the cells that changed. An unchanged log builds the same bytes, so it makes no commit. The log’s watcher runs it once a night, after its normal poll: . | Read the log a tab or two at a time (one read of a whole log is too large): get_spreadsheet with includeGridData and the fields in ARCHIVE_FIELDS, one range per tab. Each read is saved to a file. | bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/review-log-archive.ts --sheets <read1> --sheets <read2> … --sheet-id <id> --repo <document repo> --log-id <id> --document <doc> --role master|contributor --title "<log name>". It prints the commit message, or unchanged. | If it changed, commit the two files on the document repository’s main, with that message, as an agent change that is not content. | . Never archived: . | hidden helper tabs (Watch, RCS joins); | the Public Comment Source tab, and any tab of submitters or contributors; | contact columns: a header naming an email, phone, address or contact is blanked; | any email address left in another cell, which is removed. | . The node records what was left out.

f76866349b63.title: Importing offline feedback
f76866349b63.content: One process for feedback written outside the master log (issue #683): an offline copy of the log, the feedback template returned with the line-numbered review PDF, or an archived workbook to restore. Run the archive first, so the master workbook is current. | Check. bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/review-log-import.ts check <returned.xlsx> --log review/public-comment/logs/<id>.json [--base <xlsx>] [--line-map library/<review version>/pdf-line-map.json] [--tab-map "Comments=Review Public Comments"] --out report.json. The returned workbook is first validated against the template. Each tab must be a tab of the log, and its headers must be the template’s. A renamed or missing column stops the import. An extra column is reported and ignored. A dropdown value outside the master’s values, or a page or line that is not in the frozen review version, rejects the row. | Sort. Every row with feedback is put in a group. Imported CS# and PC# numbers are hints, never keys. | Group | When | . | Add to existing | same number and same title: the changed human cells | . | Conflict | same number, another title (the number is wrong or reused); or a cell changed both offline and in the master since the copy was taken | . | Possible duplicate | no such number, but the same words as another row | . | New | none of these: the master gives it a number | . | Rejected | it failed validation | . --base is the archived workbook the copy was taken from (git show <commit>:<file>). With it, a cell changed only in the master is kept. Without it, a filled master cell may only be extended offline, and any other change to it is a conflict. | A person selects. Post the review list the check printed and ask which rows to import. Give the lettered or numbered choices, with a recommendation: usually every Add and New, no Conflict. | Plan. review-log-import.ts plan report.json --log <node> --select <numbers> [--accept-conflicts] --out plan.json gives the cell writes: A1 range and value, human columns only. A new row goes below the last row, and the sheet’s script numbers it. A new comment from the PDF feedback template has only the script’s columns (page, line, comment). It is not typed into the sheet. It goes to --intake-out <csv> for public-comment.ts import --channel comment-matrix, which numbers and places it. That CSV may hold names, so it stays out of the repository. | Write the planned cells to the master log, and nothing else. Editor (orange), agent (green) and script (grey) cells are never written. The watcher then picks the new feedback up as usual. | .

84eda038d63f.title: Published with the document’s site
84eda038d63f.content: scripts/review-sheet-site.ts --out <site> (package script site:review-sheet in a folio, a sourceSteps entry of its site build) writes <site>/review-sheet/: the generic Code.gs, each review/<mode>/sheet-sync.json as <mode>.config-rows.json, review-sheet.jsonld (the script as schema:SoftwareSourceCode with its SHA-256 and commit; each document’s settings as a schema:Dataset linked to its sheet and to the Tool), and an index.html with the setup steps and the SHA-256 to check a pasted copy against. Point people there rather than sending the file.

e6ef35be1d0d.title: Trusting the script
e6ef35be1d0d.content: A copy of a sheet carries its Apps Script, so anyone starting from a template should know what they are running. | Nothing runs until the sheet’s owner allows it. The owner runs installTriggers; Google then shows the scopes, and the triggers run as the owner, whoever’s edit fires them. So an editor’s edit makes owner code read what they typed: the script therefore never writes typed text as a formula (asText, q), and touches only this sheet. | Security review. tools/review-sheet-sync/security-review.md records the threat model and findings F1 to F10, each fixed with a test or accepted with its reason. Re-review on any new write sink, service, or editor-writable tab. | The agent caps new issues (finding F6): it opens a change set’s issue only for a row with a Title or feedback text, and asks a person before opening more than 20 in one sync. | This sheet only. The template starts with @OnlyCurrentDoc, so the consent screen asks for “this spreadsheet”, not all of the owner’s spreadsheets. The script uses only SpreadsheetApp, PropertiesService, LockService and ScriptApp: no UrlFetchApp, mail or Drive, so it sends nothing out. review-sheet-security.test.ts fails if one of those, or eval/new Function, appears. | Three permissions, one file. Google works out a script’s permissions from its code, and @OnlyCurrentDoc narrows the spreadsheet one to this sheet. So the consent screen asks for exactly three: this spreadsheet, the script’s own triggers, and its menu. tools/review-sheet-sync/appsscript.json records those three for the security test, which fails if the code would need more. It is a record, not a file to paste. | Plain ASCII. The built script escapes every non-ASCII character, so a paste cannot mangle it. The build prints its SHA-256; compare it with the pasted copy. | Wrong sheet. Pasted into a sheet it was not built for, it stops with a message naming the config and tab it expected, before installing triggers. | Check a copy against its source. The script is the same for every document, so one review covers all copies. Its header names the folio-assistant-core commit it was built from. Build again at that commit with the folio’s config and compare; or ignore the copied script and paste one you built yourself. | “Google hasn’t verified this app.” Bound scripts are unverified, so the owner clicks Advanced to continue. Publishing as a verified Workspace add-on would remove the warning. | .

9771b8d74f13.title: Drafting mode: editors’ and contributors’ feedback
9771b8d74f13.content: Before a document goes to public comment, editors and contributors give feedback on the working draft. That needs a simpler sheet: no Public Comment Source, no Review Public Comments, no TWGs. Each row of feedback is a change set (CS: a list of related comments on one topic), and each change set gets a GitHub issue. Tabs. | tab | who writes | columns | . | Contributor Feedback | people, plus the Apps Script | one row per change set. Grey, mechanical: Change-set (the script gives a used row the next CS-nnn once; it stays with the row). Blue, people: Title; Selected Sections (a multi-select dropdown of the document’s table of contents, each section indented under its chapter by three U+2800 blanks per level, since a dropdown cannot nest; not real spaces, because Sheets trims a multi-select cell and the first chip would lose them and read as Invalid; plain, because a dropdown chip cannot carry a link); any number of Contributor Feedback (…) columns, one per contributor, with their initials or name in the brackets (e.g. Contributor Feedback (CL); the script reads every column whose header is Contributor Feedback or starts Contributor Feedback (); Disposition (a dropdown: Pending, Accepted, Partially accepted, Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate, Out of scope), the committee’s verdict on the row. Orange, editors: Ready for agent (Yes, No, Completed), Ready for merge (Yes/No). Grey, by the script: Section links (each selected section on its own line, linked to its place on the document page, like the Sections column of the public-comment log). Green, by the agent: Feedback (agent), right of Ready for merge, the agent’s proposed direction (not a person’s feedback: the script leaves it out of the Contributor Feedback columns, and it decides nothing). Green, by the script from Agent: Issue (<repo>#n, linked), Agentic status (as in public-comment mode: one line per PR, <repo>#n (status, completed) · what it changed), Staging review (a “review” link to the change set’s review page on its staging preview, branches/<branch>/en/review/, while its PR is open), Agentic status (filter) (the change set’s status as one plain value, for the “By agentic status” filter view) | . | Agent | the agent only | one row per change set: Change-set, Issue (URL), Agentic status, Pull request (change set), What the PRs changed (change set), Agent completed (UTC, change set), Staging review page (change set), Feedback basis (change set). The agent writes it as each step completes, by the steps of the review-sheet-agent-columns skill; a drafting sheet has no per-comment rows, so only its change-set columns apply | . | TOC (hidden) | the script | the Sections dropdown’s list and each entry’s link. Rewritten on every refresh, so it follows the document | . Colours as in public-comment mode: grey mechanical, blue human, orange editor gates, green agent-derived. Built from the folio’s review-anchors.json: each chapter (Ch 3 Digital Transformation Approach), each numbered section (3.1 DIIG alignment) and each unnumbered section, prefixed by its chapter (Ch 3 · Objectives and key messages). A multi-select cell joins its choices with , , so commas in titles become ;. Each links to sectionUrl + the anchor (sec:3-1, chap:<dir>), which the document page carries as element ids. Config, review/drafting/sheet-sync.json: . { "mode": "drafting", "anchors": "folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json", "sectionUrl": "en/<doc>/#" } . Write the URLs relative to the folio’s site: the build resolves them against iriBase in the folio’s <instance>.json (e.g. https://litlfred.github.io/dth-hrh/), so no organisation name is written in sheet-sync.json and a folio that moves changes one iriBase and rewrites its Config. An absolute https:// URL is taken as written. tabs and columns (draft, draftAgent) override the headers as in public-comment mode. Write its Config with --config review/drafting/sheet-sync.json and install as above. The Sections dropdown is a data validation “dropdown from a range” on TOC!A2:A with Allow multiple selections ticked (step 6 below). Without the tick, a cell with two or more sections shows “Invalid: Input must fall within specified range”. The agent’s part: every change set has an issue. On each sync, for every Contributor Feedback row with a Change-set: . | If the Agent tab has no row for it, add one (Change-set, Agentic status Not started). | If that row has no Issue, open a GitHub issue in the folio’s repository: title CS-nnn: <Title> (or the first feedback line while Title is empty), body the linked sections, every Contributor Feedback (…) cell verbatim, and a link back to the sheet row. Write its URL into Issue. | When feedback is added to a row later, comment the new text on its issue. | Propose a direction in Feedback (agent) for every new row (from an issue, a person or a TWG workbook) and whenever the row changes, whoever changed it. The watcher does this on its next wake (skill review-log-watch, step 5). A question for people goes there too, as a Decision needed: block (§”Inputs and outputs”). On each sync compute feedbackBasis(header, row) (tools/review-sheet-sync/feedback-issue.ts: a short hash of Title, Selected Sections and the people’s Contributor Feedback columns). Where it differs from the Agent tab’s Feedback basis (change set), or the proposal cell is empty (a person clears it to ask for a fresh one), write a new proposal and the new basis. The script’s own writes (ids, links, tree marks) do not change the basis. | Work a change set only when Ready for agent is Yes; its PRs say Closes #n for the change set’s issue, and go to Agent’s PR columns. | When you pick a row up, say so first: set its Agent status to Working and put the URL of your conversation (the session, thread or PR discussion) in Agent conversation (change set). Agentic status then opens with An agent is working on it: conversation, linked. The script finds that column by header; on a sheet that lacks it, the agent adds it at the right of the Agent (change sets) tab. | . Title is the people’s on both kinds of sheet: the agent never writes it. In public-comment mode a Title-only row on Review Change Sets is a new change set, and the agent’s title is only the first value of a row it adds (skill review-log-watch, “Change sets people make”). Feedback from the site. A folio with .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/block-feedback.yml (copy the shared templates/issue-forms/block-feedback.yml) gets 📣 feedback links that open that form with Content, Section, Block, page and Source prefilled; the contributor picks a Type and writes Comment and Proposed change. On each sync the agent lists open issues labelled feedback that no Agent row names, and for each appends a Contributor Feedback row from tools/review-sheet-sync/feedback-issue.ts (feedbackRow): Sections the block’s TOC entry, Title a draft (<section>: <first sentence>, which people may rewrite), Contributor Feedback @login (Type): comment plus Proposed: …. The script then gives it a CS id, and the agent writes the issue’s URL into that change set’s Agent row: the feedback issue is the change set’s issue, so step 2 above opens none. A comment added to the issue later is added to the row’s next empty Contributor Feedback cell. Linked templates. Each mode keeps one template sheet in the informatics.avengers Drive, laid out as above, script installed, no rows. A new document starts from its “make a copy” link (table at the end); then the agent writes the new document’s Config tab, and the owner runs installTriggers. The script in the template needs no change. Locks in a template and its copies: every cell is locked to the owner except the blue, human-controlled columns, and the heads of the Contributor Feedback (or Committee Feedback) columns, where each contributor writes their initials. The lock covers the other headers, the grey mechanical and green agent-derived columns, the Config tab, the Agent tab and the hidden TOC. The orange Ready-for-agent and Ready-for-merge columns have a lock of their own, “Ready columns: editors”, which starts with only the owner; the owner adds each document editor to it in each copy (step 4 below). Setting up a sheet for a new document . The owner (informatics.avengers) does steps 1 to 6; the agent does step 3. | Copy the template. Open the “make a copy” link for the mode (table at the end), name the copy “ Contributor Log" or " Public Comment Log", and keep it in the informatics.avengers Drive. A file copy keeps tabs, colours, dropdowns, locks and the script. **Always copy the file** (File, then Make a copy); never build a log by copying tabs into a blank spreadsheet, which leaves the script behind. The owner keeps the latest `dist/Code.gs` pasted into both templates, so a copy starts current. | Share it. Share > add contributors or reviewers as Editor. The locks still keep them to the blue columns. | Link it to the repository (agent). Give the agent the copy’s URL and the document’s repository. The agent follows “Linking a sheet to a repository” below. Until it does, Config holds only its Instructions, Key and EDITORS rows and the Selected Sections dropdown is empty. The sheet says what to do next: the first line of each tab’s Instructions starts with ⚠ and names the next step, “Not set up yet. Step 1 of 2: ask the agent to link this sheet …” (the templates carry it, so a copy starts with it), then, once linked, “Almost set up. Step 2 of 2: choose Folio Assistant, then Install”. A short toast says the same when the sheet opens, and every run of an unlinked sheet stops with “Ask the agent to link this sheet to its document: give it this sheet’s link (ID …)”. Once installed (the timerMinutes document property installTriggers sets), the ⚠ line goes and each tab’s Instructions ends with a Document: <site> Repository: <repo> line; Config has an Instructions - Links row with the site, the repository and the sheet’s settings file. | Name the editors (owner). Type their emails in Config’s orange EDITORS row, or leave it empty so only the owner can set the Ready columns (below). | Install the script: §”Installing the script, step by step” below. A copy of the template already holds the script, so the paste is needed only when the script changes; installTriggers is needed in every copy, because triggers and the owner’s permission do not copy. A copy keeps the version it was made with: when Code.gs changes, paste it again into each sheet in use, and into the template. | Drafting only: finish the Selected Sections dropdown. installTriggers adds the rule (a dropdown from TOC!A2:A) when the column has none, and leaves an existing one alone (a rewrite would clear its tick). One setting is a person’s, once per sheet: . | click the column letter above “Selected Sections” to select the column; | choose Data, then Data validation; | open the rule for that column (the sidebar lists it by its range, such as 'Contributor Feedback'!E2:E1000, as “Dropdown (from a range)”); | under Advanced options, check that Display style is Chip; | tick Allow multiple selections; | press Done. | . The tick is greyed out unless the style is Chip. A rule that Apps Script writes (requireValueInRange) gets the Arrow style, which Apps Script cannot change. The agent therefore sets the style through the Sheets API at setup, and whenever a log’s rule reads customUiMode: ARROW: setDataValidation with the same ONE_OF_RANGE condition and "showCustomUi": true, "customUiMode": "CHIP", "strict": false. The API reads the tick (condition.allowMultipleSelections) but sets it only for ONE_OF_LIST rules, so ticking it on the range rule stays the person’s step. installTriggers cannot check either directly. It shows the steps in a 30-second toast unless it has evidence they are done: a cell already holding two sections from the list (or dropdownDone). It is a toast, never a dialog: a dialog waits for an answer in the sheet, and an Install run from the Apps Script editor then hangs until Apps Script stops it at 6 minutes (“Exceeded maximum execution time”). Only the menu’s “Which version is this?” opens a dialog. Copies made after the template has them keep them. The same steps are in the Config tab’s Instructions - Dropdown row; the script ignores that row. | . Installing the script, step by step . For the sheet’s owner, once per sheet. The Config tab’s Instructions - Install script row carries the same steps and links here. | Get the latest Code.gs. Open dist/Code.gs on GitHub and press Copy raw file (the two-squares button at the top right of the code), or open the raw file, select all and copy. It is the build of review-sheet.gs on core’s main, rewritten by build-review-sheet-script.ts --dist; a test fails when it is stale. | Open the editor. In the sheet: Extensions, then Apps Script. It opens in a new tab. “Sorry, unable to open the file at this time” (in German, “Datei kann derzeit nicht geöffnet werden”) means the browser is signed in to several Google accounts and Apps Script opened under the default one (/u/0/), which cannot see the sheet: use a private window with only the owner’s account, or change /u/0/ in the failing address to /u/1/, /u/2/, and so on. | Name the project after the sheet. Click Untitled project at the top left, type the spreadsheet’s own name (e.g. “DTH-PC Contributor Log”), and press Rename, so it is found by name in script.google.com, where bound projects are listed apart from their sheets. | Paste. Click Code.gs in the Files list on the left. Select all (Ctrl+A, or Cmd+A on a Mac), delete, paste, and save (Ctrl+S or Cmd+S, or the disk icon). Code.gs is the only file to paste: leave the project’s manifest as it is. | Run installTriggers. Reload the sheet and choose Folio Assistant, then Install. Or, in the editor, the function list next to Run and Debug shows installTriggers (it is the first function, so the default; not onOpen, which only adds the menu); press Run. | Allow it. Review permissions, pick the owner’s account. Google shows “Google hasn’t verified this app. The app is requesting access to sensitive info in your Google Account.” That is expected for a sheet’s own script, which Google never verifies: press Advanced, then **Go to (unsafe)**, then **Allow** ([why](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/7454865)). | Check it. The log shows “Execution completed”. Back in the sheet tab, reload: a Folio Assistant menu appears; Folio Assistant, then Refresh now, checks it. | Drafting sheets only: tick Allow multiple selections on the Selected Sections dropdown (step 6 of “Setting up a sheet for a new document”). | . Updating later: steps 1, 2 and 4, then Folio Assistant, then Refresh now; the automatic refresh stays installed. Sheets may run older builds: Folio Assistant, then Which version is this? shows the build the sheet runs (SCRIPT_VERSION, the stamp on the script’s header line), the Code.gs copy page, and “✓ Up to date” or “New build available” by comparing with the Config tab’s CFG.LATEST_BUILD. The agent writes LATEST_BUILD (the content stamp of the build it publishes, latestBuild()) with the Config rows, so rewrite each sheet’s Config when a new build goes out. The script never fetches. The menu is named Folio Assistant and ends with About Folio Assistant, which points to https://litlfred.github.io/folio-assistant/; the same link is the last line of each tab’s Instructions. The library builds the menu (addMenu) and the stub asks it, so every sheet shows the same menu and a rename needs no new stub. A stub that builds its own “Review links” menu is out of date: paste dist/Stub.gs over it once. A copy of the template needs none of this: the script came with the file. Reload the copy, choose Folio Assistant, then Install, and allow it as in step 6. The menu runs installTriggers, so the editor is never opened. Renaming the bound project (step 3) is optional: a copied project is named “Copy of …” by Google. One library, a stub in each sheet . The code lives once, in a standalone Apps Script project, Folio Review Library, owned by the sheets’ owner, and every sheet runs its latest code (HEAD). Each sheet keeps only dist/Stub.gs, which never changes. Setting the library up, once: . | At script.google.com, New project; name it Folio Review Library. | Replace its code with dist/Code.gs; save. | Project settings (the gear): copy the Script ID. The library is 1us7_ApIq_XvDG-V1XtqdcyHucF0hSlST0qracv1Tw9KTb4-lAFvK1bMQ; the Config tab’s install steps and the stub name it. | . Each sheet, once (templates first, so copies inherit it): . | Extensions, then Apps Script. Replace Code.gs with dist/Stub.gs; save. | Libraries +: paste the Script ID, Look up, Version HEAD (Development mode), Identifier Review, Add. | In the sheet, Folio Assistant > Install. | . An update needs no paste. The library also holds dist/Updater.gs; updateFromGitHub, run from the library’s editor, fetches dist/Code.gs from main and writes it over the library’s Code.gs through the Apps Script API, leaving the library’s other files alone. It refuses anything that is not the review-sheet script (an error page, the stub) and logs “Updated to <version>” or “Already current”. There is no timer: an update runs when the owner runs it. Every sheet runs the new code from its next open, edit or timer. Adding the updater, once: . | Turn on the Apps Script API at https://script.google.com/home/usersettings. | In the library, Files +, Script, name it Updater; paste dist/Updater.gs; save. | Project settings: tick “Show appsscript.json manifest file in editor”, then replace appsscript.json with dist/library-appsscript.json (it adds the script.projects and script.external_request scopes); save. | Pick updateFromGitHub in the function list, Run, and allow it. | . After that an update is step 4 alone. Without the updater, an update is one paste of the new dist/Code.gs into the library. “Which version is this?” reports the library’s stamp. The stub hands its services over (Review.init) because a library has no spreadsheet of its own, so its document properties, document lock and triggers would not be the sheet’s. The stub passes its own PropertiesService, LockService and ScriptApp, and the triggers it installs name the stub’s functions. Pasted straight into a sheet, Code.gs still works alone: without init it uses the sheet’s services. HEAD runs only for people with edit access to the library. The triggers run as the owner who installed them, so that is the owner alone; an editor who uses Refresh now by hand needs the library shared with them as an editor. Linking a sheet to a repository . A copied sheet knows nothing about its document until the agent links it. Linking is repository work first and sheet work second, in this order: . | The folio has a section list. A drafting sheet’s dropdown is the document’s chapters and sections, read from folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json. The folio’s package.json declares review:anchors and check:review-anchors, both running folio-assistant-core/scripts/review-anchors-from-folio.ts --document <doc>. A document seeded from a library file adds `–library --source --source-label `; one authored from scratch (dth-pc, dth-sc) leaves all three out. Run `review:anchors` and commit the file. A new document folio declares both scripts from its first commit. | The folio names the sheet, and the rows are built: one command. From the folio’s root, with the link the person pasted: bun run folio-assistant-core/tools/review-sheet-sync/build-review-sheet-script.ts --link <sheet link or id> --document <doc> --out config-rows.json --toc-out toc-rows.json. It writes review/drafting/sheet-sync.json ({"mode":"drafting","anchors":"folio/<doc>/review-anchors.json","sectionUrl":"en/<doc>/#","sheet":"<spreadsheet id>"}; an existing file keeps its settings and only gets the new sheet), then the rows. The site and repository links come from the folio’s iriBase (https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/ is https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>); a folio on another host sets "repository" in sheet-sync.json. Public comment, or to rebuild after a structural change: --config review/<mode>/sheet-sync.json instead of --link. | The agent writes the sheet. With the Sheets connector, it writes the rows from step 2: the whole Config tab from A1, keeping the sheet’s EDITORS value (the Instructions - Links row sits above Key, so the CFG, COLS and DATA rows land below EDITORS), and for drafting the TOC rows into the TOC tab from A1. The connector writes values, not colours, so the agent also colours Config: the Key row a Grey header (#b7b7b7, bold), EDITORS Orange (#f4b26b), and CFG, COLS, DATA and their continuation rows Grey (#efefef), and fits the Instructions rows’ heights to their text (a Sheets API autoResizeDimensions; an inserted row otherwise inherits its neighbour’s height). Every refresh re-applies these (styleConfig), so a sheet the script runs in heals on its own. The TOC rows are exactly what the script’s refresh writes, so the dropdown works before anyone pastes the script. | The agent says what is left for a person: paste Code.gs and run installTriggers (step 5 above), and tick Allow multiple selections (step 6). | . When the branch carrying the folio is not merged yet, the agent may run steps 1 and 3 from that branch without pushing to it, and write the sheet; the branch’s owner commits the anchors and sheet-sync.json. Re-run step 3 after any structural change to the document (a section added, moved or renamed). Who may set the Ready columns: the EDITORS row. Everyone who works in a log is shared as Editor; protected ranges decide what each can change. Blue columns are open to all of them. The orange Ready for agent and Ready for merge columns are for editors only, and the owner names them in the Config tab’s EDITORS row, column B: plain emails, no names, one per line (Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter starts a line inside a cell), or separated by commas or semicolons. The format is spelled out, with an example, in the Instructions - Editors row and in a note on the cell itself. Anything that is not an email is left out, and the refresh names it in a toast. installTriggers and Folio Assistant > Refresh now lock each Ready for ... column to the owner plus those emails, under a protection the script owns and rebuilds each time (other protections are left alone). An empty row locks them to the owner alone, which is how every new sheet starts; a Config with no EDITORS row leaves them as they are. Both templates carry the Orange EDITORS row, empty. EDITORS is the one Config row a person keeps: the agent writes it empty and keeps the sheet’s value whenever it rewrites the tab, and the emails never go into sheet-sync.json, which is committed. To delegate who decides, the owner can add a delegate to the Config tab’s protection, or send the agent the list. The Instructions rows. Every visible tab opens with an Instructions row that says what that tab is for and how it works, in that tab’s own terms; tabInstructions() in the builder writes the text for each tab. On a people’s tab (RPC, RCS, Contributor Feedback) the row is frozen with the header and grey like it, a lighter grey than the header. Its first line is the colour key: Column colours: then one phrase per colour, in the order Blue, Green, Orange, Grey, worded for the mode by colourKey() and naming no colour (§”Sheet conventions”): . | Blue: input by people, named by their process role: the Feedback Review Committee in public-comment mode, the Authoring Committee in drafting mode; | Green: the agent; | Orange: an Editor (the Ready for ... columns); | Grey: the script. | . Then come the steps for that tab, one per line, naming columns, never colours. On a change-set tab they are the human-to-agent workflow, worded by process role: people write their feedback, the agent proposes, an Editor sets Ready for agent, the agent opens one pull request for the row whose Staging review opens the changes, new feedback marks the proposal stale, a second reviewer checks the dispositions and the QA report, and an Editor sets Ready for merge and the agent merges. On Review Public Comments the steps say that decisions are made per change set. Last come the filter views, and a link to the harness’s page for the process the sheet runs: public-comment.html for public comment and contributor-feedback.html for drafting, under en/cat-harness/processes/ on the folio-assistant site (processPage(); CFG.PROCESS overrides it). The first cell reads Instructions, and the text is one merged cell across the rest of the row. The script reads any leading rows whose first cell starts Instructions (or Colour key) as for people: the header is the row after them, and every write, lock and edit range starts below the header. Insert the row only after the sheet runs a Code.gs that knows it; an older script reads the legend as the header and finds no columns. Filter views and protections start at the header row, so shift them down by one row when the row is inserted. A filter view’s custom formula does not move when a column is inserted, so rewrite it. The Config tab keeps its Instructions short, one subject per row, so no row is taller than the window: Instructions (the tab’s purpose: nothing here needs you unless you install the script), Instructions - Install script (setupSteps(): copy Code.gs, Extensions > Apps Script, name the project after the spreadsheet, paste and save, run installTriggers, allow it, reload), on a drafting sheet Instructions - Dropdown (dropdownSteps()), and Instructions - Editors (editorSteps()), then the Key | Value header. Its rows are not frozen. The EDITORS row is Orange, like the Ready columns it controls, because a person keeps it; the rows the agent writes stay grey. The script reads Config keys by name, so it ignores these rows. A stale proposal hands control back to an Editor. When a row’s proposal turns stale (a blue cell changed since the agent wrote it), the script sets that row’s Ready for agent from Yes to No, once, on the turn. The agent does not act on the row until an Editor sets Yes again, which is the signal to update the row’s pull request. A Yes set while the row is still stale stays. One row, one branch, one active pull request. A change-set row keeps one branch for its whole life, and at most one pull request is open on it. Every later agent run pushes to that branch and updates that PR, so the row’s Staging review link stays the same. If the PR is closed and the committee or contributors want the work back, the agent reopens it, or opens a new PR on the same branch when it cannot be reopened. It never starts a second branch for the row. Each earlier PR stays listed in the row’s Agentic status, one line per PR. Filter views. Each template carries saved filter views, which copy with it. Use Data > Filter views, never a plain filter: a plain filter changes the view for everyone, a filter view only for whoever opens it. Each view is named for who uses it and what it shows. | sheet | view | who | shows | . | drafting: Contributor Feedback | Open | everyone | rows with a Title, Ready for merge not Yes | . |   | Needs contributor feedback | contributors | rows with a Title and every Contributor Feedback column empty | . |   | Waiting for editor (Ready for agent not Yes) | editors | rows with a Title, Ready for agent not Yes | . |   | Merge decision due (PR open, not merged) | editors | Agentic status (filter) is PR open, Ready for merge not Yes | . |   | Needs you (answer the agent’s question) | editors, owner | Agentic status (filter) starts with “Needs you” | . |   | Stale (agent proposal or staging out of date) | owner | the agent proposal starts with ⚠, or the staging link says stale | . |   | Decided (Ready for merge Yes) | everyone | Ready for merge is Yes | . |   | By agentic status (pick values) | everyone | every row; pick values in the Agentic status (filter) column’s filter (a plain copy of the change set’s Agent status) | . | public comment: Review Change Sets | Change sets: the same eight | as above | on its own columns; “Needs architect feedback” checks the three Committee Feedback (initials) columns | . | public comment: Review Public Comments | Comments: Open (no Disposition) | everyone | a No., Disposition empty | . |   | Comments: No change set yet | review coordinator | a No., Change Set empty | . |   | Comments: Needs architect feedback | the Feedback Review Committee | a No., every Committee Feedback (initials) column empty | . |   | Comments: Decided (Disposition set) | everyone | Disposition filled | . The “needs feedback” and “stale” views use a custom formula that names columns by letter, so a column move breaks them: after moving columns, the agent checks each view’s formula against the headers. A filter view covers the rows the tab had when the view was made; when rows are added past that, widen its range (Data > Filter views > the view > Options > Update range). Keeping the section list current (agent). The dropdown’s list is the hidden TOC tab, and the script writes it from DATA.TOC in the Config tab on every refresh. So when the document’s chapters or sections change (any PR that changes review-anchors.json, the same moment review:anchors runs), the agent rebuilds the Config rows (--config review/drafting/sheet-sync.json --out config-rows.json) and writes them into each drafting sheet the folio names, in the same change. Nobody edits the TOC tab by hand. How picks stay valid. On each refresh the script repairs Selected Sections before anything else: . | the pick | what the script does | . | a current section, with or without its indent (or a “└ “ mark) | rewrites it to the dropdown’s name, indent included | . | a section renamed or renumbered since it was picked | finds it by its anchor (the TOC tab’s column C keeps the anchors of the names it offered before) and rewrites it to the new name | . | a section no longer in the document | keeps it, so nothing a person chose is lost, and adds a line in Section links: ⚠ “" is not in the document now: pick its section again | . So “Invalid” after a document change clears by itself at the next refresh, except for a section that was removed, which a person repicks. Change-set ids. Any row a person has filled in gets the next CS-nnn at the next refresh, whichever column they started in. A cell holding only “No” (a Yes/No dropdown’s default) and the script’s own columns do not count. Selected Sections shows “Invalid”. Three causes: a pick of a section removed from the document (Section links flags it; pick again); a cell with several sections where the rule does not allow multiple selections (tick it, step 6); or a cell that carries links. Sections must be plain text, the links belong in Section links: clear the cell’s formatting (Format > Clear formatting) and the script keeps it plain. Check it. Folio Assistant > Refresh now. In drafting mode a filled-in row gets a CS id and its picked sections appear, linked, in Section links; in public-comment mode each No. becomes a link. An error names what is missing: no Config tab, a Config row, or a tab the Config names. | mode | template (owned by informatics.avengers) | make a copy | . | public-comment | Folio Assistant - Public Comment Review Template, 14PtLd2U_tBQV5OHoEEVRJK1EKfsbZEBPP_MIqo2E3o4 | https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14PtLd2U_tBQV5OHoEEVRJK1EKfsbZEBPP_MIqo2E3o4/copy | . | drafting | Folio Assistant - Contributor Template, 1PtcNJgLQIA1BjapU51pAQzqQjGylBHYNKlCPzZkwVag | https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PtcNJgLQIA1BjapU51pAQzqQjGylBHYNKlCPzZkwVag/copy | . A copy keeps tabs, colours, dropdowns and formulas. It does not keep protected ranges (re-add them: Agent whole tab; the grey and green columns), and its TOC tab is empty until the script’s first refresh. A document’s own sheet is named in its sheet-sync.json as sheet (the spreadsheet id), so the agent’s sync knows where to read and write.

d8a8ca2ba9f3.title: Saturation meta-merge — drain the queue when the runners are full
d8a8ca2ba9f3.content: Skill saturation-meta-merge: When the CI runners have been full for a long time, drain a repository’s ready PRs in one step: hold the swarm, cancel the queued PR runs, stack every admitted PR onto one meta-merge branch with merge commits, and land that branch on main without waiting for CI, on the owner’s card that names each PR. Then re-run main’s checks and report. Use for “runners are full”, “cancel everything and merge what’s ready”, “meta-merge”, “consolidate the queue”, and when the queue has not moved for an hour or more. Named by: Guideline Updates . This is an owner-invoked exception to merge-queue and merge-to-main. Normally every PR lands on its own green CI through merge:guard. When the runners are full, that rule is what stops the queue: each PR waits for a runner, and then a newer push to main makes its result stale. A meta-merge trades per-PR CI for one CI run on main after landing. It is only run when the owner asks for it, and on a card that names every PR. The process is sdlc/processes/saturation-meta-merge.bpmn (Process_SaturationMetaMerge), called from the merge manager’s watch loop (merge-manager-watcher).

305c128da610.title: Trigger
305c128da610.content: Offer the meta-merge, but do not run it, when either of these holds on a repository: . | PR runs have been queued for 60 minutes or more and no PR has landed in that time, or | the queue has 10 or more runs across the repositories the swarm shares, and the owner says the runners are full. | . Measure it with gh api "repos/<o>/<r>/actions/runs?status=queued" and the created_at of the oldest run. Offering it is a card (step 3). Running it is the owner’s tap.

578396bfe096.title: Steps
578396bfe096.content: . | Hold the swarm. Message every sibling thread that pushes to the repositories in scope: no new pushes, PRs, merges, run cancels or re-runs there until you post meta-merge done. Ask the coordinator to pass the hold on to any thread you cannot reach. A sibling that owns a PR in the batch names the head it wants merged. Check that the head you fetch is that head. | Dry run. Run the script (below) without PUSH=1 on each repository. It builds claude/meta-merge-<date> from origin/main and merges each PR head with --no-ff, in order. It skips a PR that: . | conflicts with main plus the PRs before it, generated paths included (the stacking rule in merge-queue), or | touches .github/workflows/ (an agent token cannot push a workflow file) or subscriptions/ (held, fixity-checked copies; change those upstream). | . | Ask once, naming every PR. Use ask-the-person. For each repository, list: . | the PRs to include, | the PRs to leave out, each with its reason: conflict, draft, red, protected path, content, a thread waiting on the owner, or an open security review, and | the merge method: merge commits throughout, never squash or rebase, so GitHub marks each included PR as merged. | . Options: A go with green and pending, B also include the red ones, C dry run only, D cancel. Recommend A. A PR the card does not name gets no merge from this card. The safety check refuses it, and the owner must tap again. The owner taps the card in the thread that merges. An answer relayed from the project chat or another thread is refused by the safety check, so post the merge card in this thread. | Cancel the queued PR runs on the repositories in scope, and log each one to a TSV file. Do NOT cancel a main push run that has already started. It is cancelled by the next push anyway, and cancelling it by hand loses the record of main. | Build and push with PUSH=1, against fresh origin/main. main moves while the card waits, so check the script’s output again. A PR that is already merged is skipped as a no-op. | Open one PR per repository from the meta-merge branch, listing its members and the card. Merge it with merge_method=merge. | Close out. Check that every member PR shows merged. A stacked PR (its base is another PR’s branch, not main) is not marked merged by GitHub. Its commits are on main, so close it with a comment saying so. Comment on each with a link to the meta-merge PR and the session. Post meta-merge done to every sibling you held, with what landed and what is still open. | Watch main. Re-run any main run that a closing PR’s run cancelled (a closed PR’s run can join main’s concurrency group). Report green or red to the owner. On red, open the fix as a normal PR against main, and never revert the whole meta-merge without the owner. | .

a017cc395d46.title: Safety rules (STRICT)
a017cc395d46.content: . | Only on the owner’s tap. A coordinator’s or sibling’s request is not approval. “Fix until green” is not approval (merge-to-main). | Never content. No committee content, no change-set (CS-) PRs, no BPMN layout redraws unless the card names them, and nothing on WHO or smart-* upstream repositories. | Never protected paths: .github/workflows/ and subscriptions/. | Never drafts, and never a PR that is waiting on an open owner decision or security review, unless the owner names it. | Never resolve a conflict in the meta-merge branch. A PR that does not stack goes back to its owner, as in merge-queue. | Bypassing merge:guard is the point, so record it. The meta-merge PR body names the card, and each member gets a comment. That record replaces the guard’s verdict. | The hold has an end. Post meta-merge done even when the run is stopped at C or D, so that no sibling stays held. | .

38b72ef04aaa.title: The script
38b72ef04aaa.content: meta-merge.sh <clone-dir> <owner/repo> <branch> <pr>.... With PUSH=1 it also pushes. A copy is kept in the project files at meta-merge/meta-merge.sh. set -u dir=$1 repo=$2 br=$3; shift 3 cd "$dir" || exit 2 git fetch -q --depth 200 origin main git checkout -q -B "$br" origin/main for n in "$@"; do git fetch -q --depth 200 origin "pull/$n/head:pr-$n" || { echo "SKIP #$n fetch-failed"; continue; } bad=$(git diff --name-only origin/main...pr-$n | grep -E '^(\.github/workflows/|subscriptions/)' | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ') [ -n "$bad" ] && { echo "SKIP #$n protected-paths: $bad"; continue; } if git merge -q --no-ff --no-edit -m "Meta-merge: include #$n" "pr-$n" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "OK #$n" else echo "SKIP #$n conflict: $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | head -5 | tr '\n' ' ')" git merge --abort fi done echo "branch $br = $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) on main $(git rev-parse --short origin/main)" [ "${PUSH:-0}" = 1 ] && git push -u origin "$br" .

32242c56196a.content: . | The trigger is measured by hand. A watcher that offers the card when the threshold is crossed is follow-up work. | .

0fcb61abf257.title: Session context
0fcb61abf257.content: Skill session-context: What a state machine tracks across a session, as against one process instance. What the record carries, why actor is required and the rest are not, why the session’s view of a node is advisory, and what a sibling session reads it for. Named by: Getting started, Authoring a document, Make the content change, Content Change and Review, Editing and HCI validation, Contributor feedback on a working draft, Record agent step, Review-log watch . A session is one actor working, from the moment it picks up until it stops. A process instance is a token’s position in one diagram. They are not the same object and the difference is load-bearing: . A session starts before any instance, may open several, switches between them, and outlives each. A session with nothing open is the commonest state there is. Model the session as a field on an instance and the first process opened owns facts that belong to the actor — and the idle session, which is most of them, becomes unrepresentable. So it is its own record, referencing instances rather than containing them. Shape: schemas/sdlc/session-context.ts. Graph typology: session-state, layer state — a session writes its own record as it goes, which is exactly what content-context-and-state-graphs means by live state.

26c7bc25f676.title: The fields — read them off the schema, never off this page
26c7bc25f676.content: SessionContextSchema in schemas/sdlc/session-context.ts is authoritative. A field list in prose beside a Zod object is a second answer, wrong the first time somebody adds a field, so this page gives no field count; the sections below say what the main fields are for.

fa1205ffcf7e.title: actor is required, and it is the point of the record
fa1205ffcf7e.content: Every other field can be recovered by looking at the repository. Open instances are in the work item graph; claimed work items carry their own status; timestamps can be reconstructed from commits. WHO is acting cannot be derived from anything. The machine keeping the session cannot infer it, which is also why log-message takes actor. A sibling session needs to know who is answerable before it touches the same work item. It is a reference with a declared flag, not an ActorDefinition. An agent may act without a node under the actors graph, and requiring one would make the field unfillable in exactly the cold-start case the record is most useful for. The two facts — an id that resolves and a name nobody declared — are kept apart because a consumer acts differently on each: an audit can follow the first to a role and a permission set, and can only quote the second. And declared is written, not inferred at read time. A reader resolving it themselves gets a different answer than the writer did if the node was added or removed in between, and the record says what was true when the session acted.

22701b0c1926.title: The rest of the fields, and what each is for
22701b0c1926.content: | field | for | notes | . | id | naming this session | stable for its life | . | startedAt / updatedAt | telling a live session from an abandoned one | ISO-8601 UTC | . | open[] | which instances this session is inside | empty is normal, not a gap | . | claimed[] | which work items this session announced | by reference, never copied | . | waitingOn | why nothing is moving | what + since, together | . open empty is the normal state. An agent answering a question, reading, or deciding what to do next is in no process at all, and process-state calls that idle rather than broken. A record that treated empty as a defect would report every reading session as one. claimed is by reference because a claim announces rather than reserves. The work item is the authority on its own status (bean-coordination (opt-in cat-harness.work-plan)); a status copied here would be free to contradict it, and a sibling reading the copy would act on a claim that had already been released. waitingOn carries since or it carries nothing. A wait with no start cannot be told from abandoned work — the same argument bean-blocking makes for requiring an expiry. what is free text on purpose: a human answer, a CI run, a sibling’s PR is an open set no enum would survive.

ffa4b27a0f20.title: The session’s view of a node is ADVISORY
ffa4b27a0f20.content: open[].atNode is what the session believes. The instance wins. The instance is the authority on its own token; this can be stale by exactly one step — the gap between a step completing and the session noticing. It is recorded anyway for two reasons. The commonest question about a session (“what is it doing”) should not need a second file read. And a disagreement between the two is itself worth seeing: a session whose view has drifted from the instance is a session that lost track, which is one of the detectors process-state names for being out of process.

b4171f53ad26.title: Who reads it, and why it is parsed rather than trusted
b4171f53ad26.content: A sibling session, deciding whether a work item is genuinely being worked or was claimed by someone who stopped. A person, asking what is in flight. The session itself on resume, in a fresh container, where the alternative is starting a second session beside the one that already exists. The writer may be an LLM playing the part of a state machine, so the shape cannot be assumed from the writer’s care. parseSessionContext() parses at the boundary, which is what makes a non-deterministic writer safe to read from. The general rule: where a machine may be played rather than executed, the schema is the contract and the parse is where it is enforced.

5b4701c1e320.title: What this is NOT
5b4701c1e320.content: Not the work plan. A work item says what is being worked on and survives the session; this says who is working and where they are right now. Delete every session record and the plan is intact. Not a log. log-message records what an actor DID at a moment, append-only. This is the current position, overwritten as it moves. A log tells you how you got here; this tells you where you are. Not interaction preferences. cat-harness/memory/interaction.json holds how a person wants to be asked — durable, read at session start, never written by a process. That is context, and this is state: the two are on opposite sides of the layer line and must not be merged, however adjacent they look. Not a store yet. The kind is registered and the shape is defined; nothing writes one, so no directory is declared for it: a declared-but-empty directory makes a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run.

79bbd839e00b.title: Playing a state machine
79bbd839e00b.content: Skill session-state-machine: An agent PLAYING a state machine rather than an engine executing one. Where the non-determinism actually lives, why the diagram stays strict, the cat-harness.processes:judgement marker that makes a judgement point countable, and what the machine must never do on the actor’s behalf. Named by: Getting started, Authoring a document, Make the content change, Content Change and Review, Editing and HCI validation, Contributor feedback on a working draft, Record agent step, Review-log watch . An agent can play a non-deterministic state machine as a tool, managing state during a human and agentic discussion. The diagram is processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn. It keeps a session’s context current across a discussion: establish who is acting, open the record, and on each turn decide whether anything changed.

fc9a160740de.title: The non-determinism is in the TRANSITIONS, not the shape
fc9a160740de.content: A machine whose shape were non-deterministic could not be drawn here. The interpreter supports nine BPMN element types and throws on the rest, on purpose: skipping an unrecognised element yields a process that runs, reports progress, and is silently not the process on the diagram. So the shape is strict and enumerable. What varies is which enabled branch the agent takes, and what it writes. An exclusive gateway carrying <cat-harness.processes:decision> is computed and workflow_complete refuses a hand-supplied outcome; one without it means the caller supplies the answer.

8099ef4c7d3f.title: Saying that a judgement is deliberate
8099ef4c7d3f.content: A gateway with no decision table can be two different things: . | somebody’s call, which no table can make, and | a table nobody has written yet. | . <cat-harness.processes:judgement reason="…"/> declares the first, with the same three rules as cat-harness.processes:no-skill on activities: the reason is required and a declaration without one does not load; it is refused on anything but an exclusive gateway; and it is refused alongside cat-harness.processes:decision, because a gateway claiming both that a table decides it and that a person does leaves a reader unable to tell which the author meant. Why this matters more than the activity case. A step with no skill is a documentation gap. A gateway with no table is a point where an LLM decides the branch — and how many of those there are, and which, is exactly the question the deterministic-to-agentic spectrum is about (deterministic-and-agentic), and a mechanism that cannot enumerate its own judgement points cannot answer it. check:workflow-refs prints the three-way split (computed, declared judgement, undeclared) from the models. Ask the checker, not this page. An undeclared gateway is a backlog entry rather than a defect: every gateway that predates the marker lands there, and a gate that failed on an un-annotated corpus would be turned off.

23d7ae8fb9db.title: What the machine must never do
23d7ae8fb9db.content: It claims nothing. No cat-harness.processes:bean appears anywhere in the diagram. The process RECORDS that an actor claimed a work item; it does not claim one. A machine that claimed on the actor’s behalf would make the claim’s owner unrecoverable — and a claim announces rather than reserves precisely so a reader can tell who announced it. It closes nothing but itself. A_CloseSession records that the actor stopped. It does not resolve work items or complete instances: those outlive the session by design, and a machine that tidied them away on exit would be asserting that work finished because somebody went away. It is advisory, not strict. An agent keeping its own session record must never be refused. A missing update is a gap in a record, not an unauthorised write — and the base content processes are the ones that gate.

4ea75678a58f.title: The two judgement points, and why each is safe to be one
4ea75678a58f.content: Gateway_ActorKnown — only the discussion says who is acting, and it rarely says so in a field. A table would need a name to read; this branch is the reading. Gateway_TurnEffect — whether a turn changed the session’s state is a reading of intent. “I might look at X later” and “start X” differ by nothing a table can key on. Both are safe to be judgement for the same reason, which will not hold everywhere: getting one wrong is recoverable. The next turn corrects it, and nothing downstream has been authorised in the meantime. Contrast the steps the base processes mark relaxable="false" — the editor seeing the findings, the decision, the write, the release authorisation — where a wrong branch authorises something that cannot be un-authorised. Recoverability is one candidate criterion for where judgement is admissible; whether it is the right one is open research (deterministic-and-agentic).

1042bc2a0629.title: Writing state a non-deterministic machine produced
1042bc2a0629.content: The record’s shape cannot be assumed from the writer’s care, because the writer is an LLM playing a part. parseSessionContext() parses at the boundary. Where a machine may be PLAYED rather than executed, the schema is the contract and the parse is where it is enforced — at the point the value crosses in.

63fa3bb323c6.title: See also
63fa3bb323c6.content: . | session-context — the record this machine keeps, and why actor is its required field. | workflow-state — which store answers which question, and why an instance and a work item must be one answer. | bpmn-processes — authoring an activity, strict vs advisory, and DMN-backed gateways. | process-state — the five detectors for being out of process. A session whose view has drifted from its instances is one of them. | .

cd6332d1973f.title: session-state-machine (skill)
